400+ AUR Packages Hijacked: What the “Atomic Arch” Campaign Means for Supply-Chain Security

StepSecurity
2026-06-13 8 use cases 3 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

On June 11th 2026, security researchers and the Arch Linux community disclosed a large-scale supply-chain attack against the Arch User Repository (AUR). Attackers hijacked more than 400 community packages and turned them into a malware delivery network. While the immediate blast radius is limited to Arch Linux systems, the campaign is a textbook example of how modern attackers compromise developers and CI infrastructure by abusing trust in open-source ecosystems.

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] AUR package manager spawning npm install of atomic-lockfile or js-digest · [LLM] AUR build context writing eBPF objects, systemd units, or cron entries
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] Build process outbound to Atomic Arch C2 (temp.sh or fardewoak GitHub) · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] Build-spawned node process reading multiple developer credential files on Arch host · [LLM] GitHub or cloud SSO sign-in from new ASN by developer whose host recently ran AUR install · Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs
AUR package manager spawning npm install of atomic-lockfile or js-digest AIInstallation High
Hunts the core execution primitive of the Atomic Arch campaign: an AUR helper or makepkg invoking npm/node to fetch the malicious atomic-lockfile (1.4.2) or js-digest Node package during PKGBUILD execution. This is the moment the hijacked package converts to live code on a developer or CI host. Rationale: Pairs the article's two strongest IOCs — the malicious npm package names (atomic-lockfile, js-digest) cited verbatim in the body and kill-chain block — with the AUR-helper parent process list (makepkg/yay/paru/pacman/pikaur/trizen/aurman). The combination of AUR-helper parent + npm child + that specific package string is effectively zero-FP outside this campaign.
ATT&CKT1195.001 T1059.004 T1059.007
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Malware analyst running the package under sandboxed makepkg/yay to reproduce
  • Internal CTF or tabletop exercise reusing the original package name
  • Defender / security tool detonation chamber repackaging the IOC for blocklist testing
  • Misconfigured CI pipeline that mirrors AUR for non-production research builds
Suppression filter
| where not (DeviceName has_any ("sandbox","detonation","malware-lab") and InitiatingProcessAccountName has_any ("analyst","researcher"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the full process tree on the host (parent AUR helper, child npm, any grandchildren) and capture the resulting node_modules path; identify the AUR package that triggered the install and the maintainer account that adopted it. 2) Contain: isolate the host from the network, kill the node/npm process tree, quarantine ~/.npm/_cacache and any node_modules under /tmp or the build directory, and treat all credentials cached on the host (SSH keys, ~/.aws/credentials, ~/.docker/config.json, ~/.npmrc, GitHub PAT, browser cookies) as compromised — start rotation immediately. 3) Hunt: pivot on the AUR package name to find other hosts that installed it in the last 30 days, search DeviceNetworkEvents for the same host reaching temp.sh / github.com/fardewoak/nodejs-argo, and check AAD/GitHub/cloud sign-ins from the affected user for new ASN or impossible-travel within the same window.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("makepkg","pacman","yay","paru","pikaur","trizen","aurman")
    or InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ ("makepkg","pacman","yay","paru","pikaur","trizen","aurman")
| where FileName in~ ("npm","node","npx")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("atomic-lockfile","js-digest")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          Parent = InitiatingProcessFileName,
          ParentCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          Grandparent = InitiatingProcessParentFileName,
          Child = FileName,
          ChildCmd = ProcessCommandLine,
          SHA256, FolderPath
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("makepkg","pacman","yay","paru","pikaur","trizen","aurman")
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("npm","node","npx")
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("atomic-lockfile","js-digest")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: AUR Package Manager Spawning npm Install of atomic-lockfile or js-digest
id: 7c3a9b2e-4f1d-4a87-9c0e-2b1a8d4f6e10
description: Detects an Arch User Repository helper (makepkg, yay, paru, pacman, pikaur, trizen, aurman) launching npm/node/npx with a command line referencing the malicious atomic-lockfile or js-digest packages used in the June 2026 'Atomic Arch' AUR supply-chain campaign.
references:
    - https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/400-aur-packages-hijacked-atomic-arch-campaign
author: thn-usecases
date: 2026/06/13
tags:
    - attack.initial_access
    - attack.execution
    - attack.t1195.001
    - attack.t1059.004
    - attack.t1059.007
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: linux
detection:
    selection_parent:
        ParentImage|endswith:
            - '/makepkg'
            - '/pacman'
            - '/yay'
            - '/paru'
            - '/pikaur'
            - '/trizen'
            - '/aurman'
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '/npm'
            - '/node'
            - '/npx'
    selection_cmd:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - 'atomic-lockfile'
            - 'js-digest'
    condition: selection_parent and selection_child and selection_cmd
falsepositives:
    - Security researcher reproducing the malicious package in an isolated VM
    - Internal red-team rebuilding the campaign for tabletop exercises
level: high
source:linux.auditd @auditd.type:EXECVE (@process.executable.path:(*/npm OR */node OR */npx)) @process.command_line:(*atomic-lockfile* OR *js-digest*)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ParentBaseFileName=/^(makepkg|pacman|yay|paru|pikaur|trizen|aurman)$/i ImageFileName=/\/(npm|node|npx)$/i CommandLine=/atomic-lockfile|js-digest/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ParentBaseFileName, ImageFileName, CommandLine, SHA256HashData], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("makepkg","pacman","yay","paru","pikaur","trizen","aurman") Processes.process_name IN ("npm","node","npx") (Processes.process="*atomic-lockfile*" OR Processes.process="*js-digest*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.process_hash
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)`
| `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("makepkg","pacman","yay","paru","pikaur","trizen","aurman") Processes.process_name IN ("npm","node","npx") (Processes.process="*atomic-lockfile*" OR Processes.process="*js-digest*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.process_hash
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)`
| `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
Build process outbound to Atomic Arch C2 (temp.sh or fardewoak GitHub) AICommand & Control High
Detects the Atomic Arch payload retrieval and credential exfiltration channel — package-manager-spawned npm/node/curl/wget reaching temp.sh (file-share egress) or github.com/fardewoak/nodejs-argo (next-stage pull). The attacker uses these during the build/install window when network egress from a package manager should be very narrow. Rationale: Combines the two C2/exfil IOCs the article and kill-chain block name explicitly (temp.sh, github.com/fardewoak/nodejs-argo) with the narrow process set that should normally make outbound calls during an AUR build (npm/node/curl/wget plus AUR helpers themselves). Either IOC alone would be moderate-FP; pairing them with the build-process initiator is high-fidelity.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1105 T1567.002
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Web.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer legitimately using temp.sh for one-off file sharing from a workstation that also happens to be a build host
  • Threat researcher fetching the attacker's GitHub repo for analysis (curl/wget to fardewoak)
  • CI mirror or proxy log that records every internal client's egress and incidentally hits temp.sh from a build node
  • DNS sinkhole or threat-intel scanner probing the IOCs from a build VLAN
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessAccountName has_any ("researcher","analyst","redteam") and DeviceName has_any ("lab","sandbox","detonation"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the full DeviceNetworkEvents + DeviceProcessEvents pair for the host showing the egress — identify the parent AUR helper, the package being built, and whether bytes flowed inbound (payload pull) or outbound (exfil). 2) Contain: block temp.sh, github.com/fardewoak/* at the proxy/firewall, network-isolate the host, kill the process tree, and treat any credentials present on the host (SSH keys, GitHub PAT, ~/.aws/credentials, browser sessions, Slack/Discord tokens, Docker creds) as exposed — initiate rotation. 3) Hunt: enumerate all hosts that resolved temp.sh or hit fardewoak in the last 30 days, cross-reference against AUR install history, and look for follow-on GitHub/npm/cloud OAuth or PAT use from new ASNs by the same users.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("npm","node","npx","makepkg","pacman","yay","paru","pikaur","curl","wget")
    or InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ ("makepkg","pacman","yay","paru","pikaur","trizen","aurman")
| where RemoteUrl has_any ("temp.sh","fardewoak/nodejs-argo","fardewoak")
    or RemoteUrl matches regex @"(?i)(^|\.)temp\.sh($|/|:)"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountDomain = InitiatingProcessAccountDomain, AccountName = InitiatingProcessAccountName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName,
          RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Protocol, ActionType
| order by Timestamp desc
ImWebSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where Url has_any ("temp.sh","fardewoak/nodejs-argo","fardewoak")
    or DstHostname has_any ("temp.sh","github.com") and Url contains "fardewoak"
| where HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent has_any ("npm","node","curl","wget","yarn") or isempty(HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent)
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcUsername, Url, DstHostname, DstIpAddr, HttpMethod, HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent, HttpRequestBodyBytes
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Build-spawned node process reading multiple developer credential files on Arch host AIActions on Objectives Medium
Hunts the Atomic Arch Rust stealer's collection phase: a node/npm process (or any short-lived binary descended from makepkg/pacman/yay/paru) reading three or more sensitive credential stores within a short window — SSH keys, ~/.aws/credentials, ~/.docker/config.json, ~/.npmrc, ~/.config/gh, or browser cookie databases. Single-file access is noisy; fan-out across categories is the signal. Rationale: The article lists the exact credential categories the Rust stealer harvests (SSH keys, ~/.aws, ~/.docker, npm tokens, GitHub CLI, Slack/Discord/Teams sessions, browser cookies). Pairing those paths with a build-context initiator (node/npm or descended from makepkg/yay/paru) and a fan-out threshold (>=3 categories) filters routine single-file reads (e.g. ssh-agent loading one key) and isolates collection-stage behaviour.
ATT&CKT1555.003 T1552.001 T1552.004 T1539
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer setup script that legitimately seeds ~/.ssh, ~/.aws and ~/.docker on a freshly imaged workstation
  • Dotfile sync tool (chezmoi, yadm) reading the same files for backup
  • Cloud CLI ('aws sso login', 'gh auth refresh') touching multiple credential stores during a single user-initiated refresh
  • node-based developer tooling (vscode-server, npm doctor) auditing local config in support workflows
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("chezmoi","yadm","stow","sso login","gh auth") and CredCategoriesTouched <= 4)
Response runbook
1) Triage: capture the node/npm process tree and command line — confirm the parent is an AUR helper or PKGBUILD shell, and that the process is short-lived (stealers exit fast). Pull which categories were touched and any subsequent writes to /tmp or /dev/shm (stage files). 2) Contain: isolate the host, kill the process, snapshot the user's home directory for IR, and treat every category touched as compromised — rotate SSH keys (revoke from authorized_keys on bastions), GitHub PATs, npm tokens, AWS access keys, and invalidate Slack/Discord/Teams sessions. 3) Hunt: pivot on the user across SigninLogs/AAD, GitHub audit, npm registry audit, and CloudTrail for use of the now-exposed tokens; check temp.sh / fardewoak egress from the same host in the same window.
let CredentialPaths = dynamic(["/.ssh/id_","/.ssh/known_hosts","/.aws/credentials","/.docker/config.json","/.npmrc","/.config/gh","/.config/Slack","/.config/discord","/.config/Code","/.mozilla/firefox","/Cookies","/Login Data"]);
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node","npm","npx")
    or InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ ("makepkg","pacman","yay","paru","pikaur","trizen","aurman")
| extend MatchedPath = tostring(array_iff(CredentialPaths, true))
| where FolderPath has_any (CredentialPaths) or FileName has_any ("id_rsa","id_ed25519","id_ecdsa","known_hosts","credentials","config.json")
| summarize CredCategoriesTouched = dcount(case(
        FolderPath has "/.ssh/", "ssh",
        FolderPath has "/.aws/", "aws",
        FolderPath has "/.docker/", "docker",
        FolderPath has "/.npmrc", "npm",
        FolderPath has "/.config/gh", "github",
        FolderPath has "/.config/Slack", "slack",
        FolderPath has "/.config/discord", "discord",
        FolderPath has_any ("Cookies","Login Data","/.mozilla/"), "browser",
        "other")),
    FileSample = make_set(strcat(FolderPath, "/", FileName), 25),
    FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp), TotalAccesses = count()
    by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| where CredCategoriesTouched >= 3
| order by LastSeen desc
let CredentialPaths = dynamic(["/.ssh/id_","/.ssh/known_hosts","/.aws/credentials","/.docker/config.json","/.npmrc","/.config/gh","/.config/Slack","/.config/discord","/.mozilla/firefox","/Cookies","/Login Data"]);
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("node","npm","npx")
| where TargetFilePath has_any (CredentialPaths)
    or TargetFileName has_any ("id_rsa","id_ed25519","id_ecdsa","known_hosts","credentials")
| summarize CredCategoriesTouched = dcount(case(
        TargetFilePath has "/.ssh/", "ssh",
        TargetFilePath has "/.aws/", "aws",
        TargetFilePath has "/.docker/", "docker",
        TargetFilePath has "/.npmrc", "npm",
        TargetFilePath has "/.config/gh", "github",
        TargetFilePath has "/.config/Slack", "slack",
        TargetFilePath has "/.config/discord", "discord",
        TargetFilePath has_any ("Cookies","Login Data","/.mozilla/"), "browser",
        "other")),
    PathSample = make_set(TargetFilePath, 25),
    FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated)
    by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| where CredCategoriesTouched >= 3
| order by LastSeen desc
source:linux.auditd (@process.executable.path:(*/node OR */npm OR */npx)) (@file.path:(*/.ssh/id_* OR */.aws/credentials OR */.docker/config.json OR */.npmrc OR */.config/gh/* OR */.config/Slack/* OR */.config/discord/* OR *Cookies* OR *"Login Data"*))

| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName], function={ collect([TargetFileName]) | count(TargetFileName, distinct=true, as=cred_cats) })
| cred_cats >= 3

AUR build context writing eBPF objects, systemd units, or cron entries AIInstallation Medium
Detects the Atomic Arch rooted-host persistence path: a process descended from makepkg/pacman/yay/paru (or a node child) writing into /sys/fs/bpf/, /etc/systemd/system/, /etc/cron.d/, or modifying shell init files. The article specifically calls out eBPF rootkit persistence and 'suspicious systemd units' as the rooted-install outcome. Rationale: Article and kill-chain block both name eBPF persistence and 'suspicious systemd units' as the rooted-install outcome. Pairing the four persistence root paths (/sys/fs/bpf, /etc/systemd/system, /etc/cron.d, shell rc files) with a node/npm or AUR-helper-descended writer process gives a single-table hunt that is broad enough to catch any of the three persistence variants but narrow on initiator.
ATT&CKT1014 T1543.002 T1053.003 T1546.004
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate Arch package installing a systemd unit through a normal pacman hook (e.g. docker, libvirt, tailscale) — the parent is pacman but the package itself is benign
  • Developer installing bpftrace/bcc/bpftool for kernel observability and exercising it for the first time
  • Dotfile management tool rewriting ~/.bashrc / ~/.zshrc during a freshly imaged workstation setup
  • Internal Ansible/Chef run pushing a new systemd unit through an over-broad parent process tree
Suppression filter
| where not (FolderPath startswith "/etc/systemd/system/" and InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("docker.service","containerd.service","libvirt","tailscaled") and InitiatingProcessParentFileName == "pacman")
Response runbook
1) Triage: inspect the written file (systemd unit body / cron entry / bpf object) — is the ExecStart pointing to /tmp, /dev/shm, or an unsigned binary? Walk the parent chain back to the AUR package and identify the maintainer / adoption history. 2) Contain: stop and disable the systemd unit (systemctl stop/disable/mask), remove the cron entry, unload the BPF program (bpftool prog show / detach), isolate the host, and treat all on-host credentials as exposed. 3) Hunt: pivot the AUR package name across the fleet (every host that installed it), look for the same persistence path written by build context in the prior 30 days, and check for outbound to temp.sh / fardewoak from those hosts.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where FolderPath startswith "/sys/fs/bpf/"
    or FolderPath startswith "/etc/systemd/system/"
    or FolderPath startswith "/etc/cron.d/"
    or FolderPath startswith "/etc/cron.hourly/"
    or FolderPath startswith "/etc/cron.daily/"
    or FolderPath has "/.config/systemd/user/"
    or (FileName in~ (".bashrc",".bash_profile",".profile",".zshrc") and FolderPath !startswith "/etc/skel")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node","npm","npx","bpftool")
    or InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ ("makepkg","pacman","yay","paru","pikaur","trizen","aurman")
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName != "root" or InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ ("makepkg","yay","paru")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName,
          ActionType, FolderPath, FileName, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
| where TargetFilePath startswith "/sys/fs/bpf/"
    or TargetFilePath startswith "/etc/systemd/system/"
    or TargetFilePath startswith "/etc/cron.d/"
    or TargetFilePath has "/.config/systemd/user/"
    or TargetFileName in~ (".bashrc",".bash_profile",".profile",".zshrc")
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("node","npm","npx","bpftool")

GitHub or cloud SSO sign-in from new ASN by developer whose host recently ran AUR install AIActions on Objectives Medium
Hunts the downstream pivot the article warns about: an attacker uses tokens stolen from an Arch developer laptop or self-hosted runner to authenticate to GitHub, npm, or cloud consoles from new geo/ASN. Correlates recent AUR helper invocations on a host (via Defender DeviceProcessEvents) with the same user's subsequent SSO sign-ins from a previously-unseen IP space. Rationale: Article explicitly states the attacker's goal is pivoting from a single Arch laptop into GitHub/npm/cloud accounts using stolen tokens. The detection joins two signals: (a) the user actually ran an AUR helper on a host in the lookback window (Atomic Arch's pre-condition) and (b) a sign-in from a previously-unseen IP to a developer-tier app afterwards. Either signal alone is weak; together they isolate the Atomic-Arch follow-on.
ATT&CKT1657 T1078.004 T1550.001
Data sourcesAuthentication.Authentication
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer travelling, switching to home/hotel IP, or moving between office and remote — appears as new ASN
  • Carrier mobile data or split-tunnel VPN changing apparent egress IP for the user
  • Cloud-provider IDE (GitHub Codespaces, Gitpod, AWS Cloud9) authenticating from a sudden new datacenter range the user has never used before
  • Newly added developer account whose 60-day IP baseline is still sparse
Suppression filter
| where not (UserAgent has_any ("Codespaces","Gitpod","Cloud9") and Country in ("United States","Ireland","Netherlands"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the user genuinely owns the new IP — message the developer out-of-band; review the sign-in's ConditionalAccess result, MFA detail, and UserAgent for non-browser tooling (gh, aws-cli, npm). Compare against the AUR install timestamp on the host. 2) Contain: revoke active sessions for the user across AAD/GitHub/npm/AWS, revoke any PATs/access keys/refresh tokens issued before the AUR install, force MFA reset, and disable any newly-created service principals/PATs in the same window. 3) Hunt: walk forward from the suspicious sign-in — repo clones, package publishes, IAM policy changes, OAuth app grants, secret reads from Vault/AWS Secrets Manager; walk backwards on the host for temp.sh / fardewoak egress and credential file fan-out.
let LookbackDays = 14d;
let AurUsers = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where FileName in~ ("makepkg","pacman","yay","paru","pikaur","trizen","aurman")
    | where isnotempty(AccountUpn)
    | summarize AurFirst = min(Timestamp), AurLast = max(Timestamp), AurHosts = make_set(DeviceName, 20) by AccountUpn;
let KnownIps = AADSignInEventsBeta
    | where Timestamp between (ago(60d) .. ago(LookbackDays))
    | summarize by AccountUpn, IPAddress;
AADSignInEventsBeta
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where ErrorCode == 0
| join kind=inner AurUsers on AccountUpn
| where Timestamp >= AurFirst
| join kind=leftanti KnownIps on AccountUpn, IPAddress
| where Application has_any ("GitHub","npm","Amazon","AWS","GitLab","Docker","Vault") or ResourceDisplayName has_any ("GitHub","npm","AWS","GitLab","Docker","Vault")
| project Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Country, City, Application, ResourceDisplayName, UserAgent, AurHosts, AurFirst
| order by Timestamp desc
let LookbackDays = 14d;
let AurUsers = Syslog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where ProcessName in~ ("makepkg","pacman","yay","paru","pikaur","trizen","aurman")
        or SyslogMessage has_any (" makepkg "," yay "," paru "," pacman -S")
    | extend SrcUser = extract(@"USER=(\S+)", 1, SyslogMessage)
    | where isnotempty(SrcUser)
    | summarize AurFirst = min(TimeGenerated), AurHosts = make_set(HostName, 20) by SrcUser;
let KnownIps = SigninLogs
    | where TimeGenerated between (ago(60d) .. ago(LookbackDays))
    | summarize by UserPrincipalName, IPAddress;
SigninLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where ResultType == 0
| where AppDisplayName has_any ("GitHub","npm","Amazon","AWS","GitLab","Docker","HashiCorp")
| extend SrcUser = tostring(split(UserPrincipalName, "@")[0])
| join kind=inner AurUsers on $left.SrcUser == $right.SrcUser
| where TimeGenerated >= AurFirst
| join kind=leftanti KnownIps on UserPrincipalName, IPAddress
| project TimeGenerated, UserPrincipalName, IPAddress, Location, AppDisplayName, ClientAppUsed, UserAgent, AurHosts, AurFirst
| order by TimeGenerated desc
source:azure.activeDirectory @evt.name:"Sign-in activity" @properties.appDisplayName:(GitHub OR npm OR Amazon* OR AWS* OR GitLab OR Docker OR HashiCorp*) -@network.client.geoip.country.iso_code:(US OR GB OR DE OR FR OR NL OR CA OR IE OR AU OR JP OR SG)
#event_simpleName=IdpAuthenticationLog (TargetAppName=/GitHub|npm|AWS|Amazon|GitLab|Docker|HashiCorp/i)
| join({ #event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/\/(makepkg|pacman|yay|paru|pikaur|trizen|aurman)$/i | groupBy([UserName], function=min(_time, as=aur_first)) }, field=UserName, include=[aur_first])
| _time >= aur_first
| groupBy([UserName, SrcIpAddr, TargetAppName], function=count())
# log group: /aws/cloudtrail
fields @timestamp, eventName, eventSource, sourceIPAddress, userIdentity.userName, userIdentity.arn, userIdentity.type, userAgent, awsRegion
| filter eventName in ["ConsoleLogin","GetCallerIdentity","AssumeRoleWithSAML","AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity"]

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT

        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")

title: Trusted Vendor Binary Launching Unusual Children
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d09
status: experimental
description: |

    spawning script-host or LOLBin children. Strongest signal when

references:

Detects deletion, renaming, or truncation of ~/Library/Biome/streams/restricted/App.MenuItem/local — the new macOS Tahoe 26 SEGB-encapsulated protobuf stream that records the literal text of user menu selections. Adversaries aware of the stream's investigative value (it preserves Compress / Move to Trash / Empty Trash narrative even after files are gone) will tamper with it to break the menu-selection timeline. Rationale: Article explicitly names the file path `~/Library/Biome/streams/restricted/App.MenuItem/local` as the new macOS Tahoe 26 SEGB-protobuf stream. Allow-listing the documented Biome daemon set (`biomed`, `biomesyncd`) makes any other writer/deleter a high-fidelity anti-forensic signal. Cross-checked against: • https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/new-macos-artifact-discovered/
ATT&CKT1070.004 T1070
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • IR / forensics team running ccl-segb extraction and moving the exported file aside
  • macOS major-version upgrade migrating or rotating Biome stream layouts
  • Third-party privacy cleaners (CleanMyMac, OnyX, Privacy Cleaner) purging ~/Library logs
  • Time Machine restore reverting Biome state to an earlier snapshot
  • User account deletion / Migration Assistant flushing ~/Library/Biome
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath !startswith "/Applications/CleanMyMac" and InitiatingProcessFolderPath !startswith "/Applications/OnyX.app" and InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("Migration Assistant","backupd")
Response runbook
1) Triage: pivot on InitiatingProcessFileName / ActingProcessName + SHA256 — Apple-signed and under /System or /usr/libexec, likely benign; unsigned binary under /Users, /tmp, /private/var/folders, or /Applications dropped <7d ago is suspect. Pull DeviceProcessEvents for the same DeviceId ±5 min for parent context. 2) Contain: if the writer is unsigned or in a user-writable path, isolate the host via Defender for Endpoint live response and preserve the surviving Biome streams plus `log show --predicate 'subsystem == "com.apple.biome"' --last 24h` before reimaging. 3) Hunt: same DeviceId for additional Biome stream tampering under /Library/Biome/streams/restricted/ (e.g. App.Activity, App.InFocus), unified-log clearing (`log erase`), and recent LaunchAgent / LaunchDaemon drops by the same process or user.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FolderPath has "/Library/Biome/streams/restricted/App.MenuItem/"
| where ActionType in ("FileDeleted","FileRenamed","FileModified")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("biomed","biomesyncd","tccd","backupd","mds_stores")
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath !startswith "/System/"
   and InitiatingProcessFolderPath !startswith "/usr/libexec/"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, ActionType, FolderPath, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessSHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where TargetFilePath has "/Library/Biome/streams/restricted/App.MenuItem/"
| where EventType in ("FileDeleted","FileRenamed","FileModified")
| where ActingProcessName !in~ ("biomed","biomesyncd","tccd","backupd","mds_stores")
| where ActingProcessCommandLine !startswith "/System/"
   and ActingProcessCommandLine !startswith "/usr/libexec/"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, EventType, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName,
          ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFileSHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Post-compromise enumeration of macOS Biome forensic streams AIActions on Objectives Medium
Detects a single process or shell session sequentially listing or reading multiple files under ~/Library/Biome/streams/ within a short window — the access pattern an attacker uses to map what user-intent telemetry (App.MenuItem and siblings) exists before exfiltration or tampering. Also catches invocation of the open-source `ccl-segb` parser referenced in the article when run outside an IR engagement. Rationale: Article calls out `ccl-segb` and the `python ccl_segb_cli.py <exportedfilename>` invocation explicitly, and names the exact directory `~/Library/Biome/streams/restricted/App.MenuItem/local`. Both are high-fidelity tokens — the parser is not pre-installed on macOS and the stream path is not a normal user-process read target. Cross-checked against: • https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/new-macos-artifact-discovered/
ATT&CKT1083 T1005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Incident response engagement: IR analyst running ccl-segb against an exported image
  • Security research / DFIR training labs on the same endpoint
  • Backup utilities (Carbon Copy Cloner, ChronoSync) walking ~/Library trees
  • Apple-signed diagnostic collection (sysdiagnose) packaging Biome streams
  • Spotlight reindexing scanning the Biome directory tree
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("sysdiagnose","spindump","CrashReporter","mdworker_shared","Carbon Copy Cloner","chronosync")
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm whether the host belongs to an active IR / forensics engagement; if not, pivot on the initiating process — unsigned binary, interactive shell (zsh/bash), or curl/wget-downloaded python script is high suspicion. 2) Contain: capture process tree and network connections from the same DeviceId in a ±15-min window; if the host shows outbound to a non-corp destination right after the enumeration, isolate via Defender live response. 3) Hunt: across the org, search for the same ccl-segb invocation or `App.MenuItem` substring on any other macOS host; pivot from the user to AAD sign-in anomalies and Login Items / LaunchAgent additions in the last 30 days.
let WindowMinutes = 5m;
let ParserHits = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("ccl_segb_cli.py","ccl-segb","App.MenuItem","/Library/Biome/streams")
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("biomed","biomesyncd")
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source="parser_or_path_referenced";
let FileFanOut = DeviceFileEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where FolderPath has "/Library/Biome/streams/"
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("biomed","biomesyncd","tccd","Finder","mdworker_shared","mds","mds_stores","backupd")
    | summarize DistinctFiles = dcount(FolderPath), FilesSeen = make_set(FileName, 25),
                FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp)
        by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, bin(Timestamp, WindowMinutes)
    | where DistinctFiles >= 5
    | extend Source = "sequential_stream_read"
    | project-rename Timestamp = FirstSeen, AccountName = InitiatingProcessAccountName;
union ParserHits, FileFanOut
| order by Timestamp desc
let WindowMinutes = 5m;
let ParserHits = ImProcessCreate
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("ccl_segb_cli.py","ccl-segb","App.MenuItem","/Library/Biome/streams")
    | where ParentProcessName !in~ ("biomed","biomesyncd")
    | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, Source="parser_or_path_referenced";
let FileFanOut = ImFileEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where TargetFilePath has "/Library/Biome/streams/"
    | where ActingProcessName !in~ ("biomed","biomesyncd","tccd","Finder","mdworker_shared","mds","mds_stores","backupd")
    | summarize DistinctFiles = dcount(TargetFilePath), FilesSeen = make_set(TargetFileName, 25),
                FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated)
        by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, bin(TimeGenerated, WindowMinutes)
    | where DistinctFiles >= 5
    | extend Source = "sequential_stream_read"
    | project-rename TimeGenerated = FirstSeen;
union ParserHits, FileFanOut
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Unauthorized read or bulk export of macOS Tahoe 26 App.MenuItem Biome stream AIActions on Objectives Medium
Detects read, copy, or archive operations against ~/Library/Biome/streams/restricted/App.MenuItem/local — the SEGB-protobuf stream that records the user's literal menu selections including text typed into Save dialogs (the article observed `u42validation`, `stolendata`, Compress, Move to Trash, Empty Trash). Attacker access to this file reconstructs the victim's intent timeline and exposes file/folder names the user typed; we want every reader that isn't an OS daemon or a known forensic tool. Rationale: Article documents the exact path `~/Library/Biome/streams/restricted/App.MenuItem/local` and shows the stream contains user-typed strings (`u42validation`, `stolendata`) plus menu narrative — high-value to an adversary reconstructing victim intent or harvesting typed filenames. Archive utilities (tar/zip/ditto/rsync) referencing the Biome path is the canonical bulk-export shape on macOS. Cross-checked against: • https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/new-macos-artifact-discovered/
ATT&CKT1005 T1217 T1119
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Apple sysdiagnose / `log collect` packaging Biome streams for support
  • Time Machine / backupd snapshotting ~/Library
  • Spotlight (mds_stores) and mdworker_shared indexing
  • Endpoint backup / DLP agents reading ~/Library
  • DFIR analyst running ccl-segb against an exported image (overlaps with UC2 — filter by engagement scope)
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("log","sysdiagnose","spindump","CrashReporter") and InitiatingProcessFolderPath !startswith "/Applications/Utilities/"
Response runbook
1) Triage: identify the reading process — Apple-signed under /System, /usr/libexec, or /Applications/Utilities is almost certainly benign (sysdiagnose, backupd); third-party signed (DLP, backup agent) check vendor and rollout; unsigned or downloaded binary is high suspicion. Inspect the parent process and recent network activity for the same DeviceId. 2) Contain: if the reader is unsigned, run from a user-writable path, or correlates with bulk archive creation (.zip/.tar in /Users/Shared, /tmp, /private/var/folders), isolate the host via Defender live response and preserve any archive on disk. 3) Hunt: query the same DeviceId for reads of sibling Biome streams (App.Activity, App.InFocus, Notification.Activity), Keychain access (`security` CLI), browser cookie / login data reads, and outbound transfer (curl/scp/rsync) within ±30 min of the Biome read.
let StreamPath = "/Library/Biome/streams/restricted/App.MenuItem/";
let ReadEvents = DeviceFileEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where FolderPath has StreamPath
    | where ActionType in ("FileOpened","FileAccessed","FileCopied")
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("biomed","biomesyncd","tccd","Finder","mds_stores","backupd","sysdiagnose")
    | where InitiatingProcessFolderPath !startswith "/System/" and InitiatingProcessFolderPath !startswith "/usr/libexec/";
let ArchiveExfil = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where FileName in~ ("tar","zip","cp","rsync","scp","ditto")
    | where ProcessCommandLine has "/Library/Biome/streams";
union ReadEvents, ArchiveExfil
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName=coalesce(InitiatingProcessAccountName, AccountName),
          ActionType, FolderPath, FileName, InitiatingProcessFileName,
          InitiatingProcessCommandLine=coalesce(InitiatingProcessCommandLine, ProcessCommandLine),
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessSHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
let StreamPath = "/Library/Biome/streams/restricted/App.MenuItem/";
let ReadEvents = ImFileEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where TargetFilePath has StreamPath
    | where EventType in ("FileOpened","FileAccessed","FileCopied","FileRead")
    | where ActingProcessName !in~ ("biomed","biomesyncd","tccd","Finder","mds_stores","backupd","sysdiagnose")
    | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, EventType, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine;
let ArchiveExfil = ImProcessCreate
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where ActingProcessName in~ ("tar","zip","cp","rsync","scp","ditto")
    | where ActingProcessCommandLine has "/Library/Biome/streams"
    | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, EventType="ProcessCreated", TargetFilePath=ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFileName=ActingProcessName, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine;
union ReadEvents, ArchiveExfil
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc

``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:

| order by TimeGenerated desc

The Hacker News
2026-06-12 17 use cases 5 techniques 5 kill-chain phases detected

Attackers took over more than 400 packages in the Arch User Repository (AUR) this week and rewrote their build scripts to install a credential stealer on any machine that built them. Atomic Arch: makepkg child spawning npm install atomic-lockfile or bun install js-digest AIDelivery High
Detects the AUR build process (makepkg) spawning npm/bun to pull the malicious atomic-lockfile or js-digest packages whose preinstall hooks drop the deps ELF. Article-specific: these two npm package names are the supply-chain pivot. Rationale: Pivots on the two explicit package names the article names as the Atomic Arch / second-wave installers (atomic-lockfile, js-digest), constrained to makepkg/shell parents so legit npm dev work doesn't fire. Cross-checked with Sonatype's Atomic Arch tracker reference. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/002/ • https://www.sonatype.com/blog
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1059.004
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Arch maintainer manually testing a benign rebuild that genuinely depends on atomic-lockfile before the package was pulled
  • Internal mirror or research VM running takedown verification scripts
  • Security researcher reproducing the campaign in a sandbox
  • AUR helper (yay/paru) running a forensics dry-run replay
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine !has "--dry-run" and InitiatingProcessCommandLine !has "--analyze"
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Pull the full PKGBUILD and .install script from the affected AUR package (look in /var/cache/pacman/, ~/.cache/yay/, ~/.cache/paru/) and check git history for the suspicious adoption commit. Capture process tree around the makepkg invocation and the host's recent AUR upgrade list. Step 2 (contain): Isolate the host from the network; if the binary executed, treat all developer credentials on the host as compromised (browser sessions, GitHub/npm/Vault tokens, SSH keys). Kill any deps process and its systemd unit. Step 3 (hunt): Search the fleet for other hosts that built the same AUR package name in the last 14 days, then enumerate /sys/fs/bpf/ for hidden_pids/hidden_names/hidden_inodes maps to flag rootkit-installed hosts requiring reimage.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("makepkg","bash","sh","zsh","fish")
| where FileName in~ ("npm","bun","node","yarn")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("install atomic-lockfile","install js-digest","atomic-lockfile@1.4.2")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, FolderPath, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("makepkg","/bin/bash","/bin/sh","/usr/bin/bash","/usr/bin/zsh")
| where TargetProcessName has_any ("npm","bun","node","yarn")
| where TargetProcessCommandLine has_any ("install atomic-lockfile","install js-digest","atomic-lockfile@1.4.2")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

description: Detects makepkg or shell parent spawning npm/bun to install atomic-lockfile or js-digest, the Atomic Arch supply-chain pivot packages.

logsource:

source:linux.auditd @auditd.type:EXECVE (@process.command_line:(*"install atomic-lockfile"* OR *"install js-digest"* OR *"atomic-lockfile@1.4.2"*)) (@process.name:(npm OR bun OR node OR yarn))

Atomic Arch: deps ELF execution by SHA256/MD5 or src/hooks/deps path AIInstallation Medium
Direct IOC hit on the Rust stealer binary deps. Article publishes SHA256 6144d433f8a0316869877b5f834c801251bbb936e5f1577c5680878c7443c98b and MD5 42b59fdbe1b72895b2951412222ebf40, plus the canonical payload path src/hooks/deps inside the npm package. Rationale: Hash IOCs are published by the article and ioctl.fail; src/hooks/deps is the canonical preinstall-hook ELF location inside the malicious npm tarball. Hits at file-create or process-execute time. Cross-checked vs MITRE T1204.002 and Sonatype Atomic Arch references. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1204/002/ • https://www.sonatype.com/blog
ATT&CKT1204.002 T1059.004
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Malware research VM intentionally detonating the sample
  • Backup/storage system retaining a known-bad cache copy that's read but not executed
  • IR scanner script comparing fleet hashes against this IOC list
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Confirm hash match in the source telemetry; if path-based, cat the file and stat it to confirm size and inode. Identify the parent process that wrote/spawned it (expect makepkg → npm/bun → node preinstall). Step 2 (contain): Isolate host; kill the deps process and any per-user/system systemd unit pointing at /var/lib/<name> or ~/.config/systemd/user/<name>.service. Step 3 (hunt): If the binary ran as root, treat the host as rootkit-capable and pull it for reimage — checking /sys/fs/bpf/ for hidden_pids/hidden_names/hidden_inodes maps. Pivot to all hosts that built the same AUR package in the last 30 days.
union
( DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where SHA256 =~ "6144d433f8a0316869877b5f834c801251bbb936e5f1577c5680878c7443c98b"
         or MD5 =~ "42b59fdbe1b72895b2951412222ebf40"
         or FolderPath has "src/hooks" and FileName =~ "deps"
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, Source = "Process", FileName, FolderPath, SHA256, MD5, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine ),
( DeviceFileEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where SHA256 =~ "6144d433f8a0316869877b5f834c801251bbb936e5f1577c5680878c7443c98b"
         or MD5 =~ "42b59fdbe1b72895b2951412222ebf40"
         or FolderPath has "src/hooks" and FileName =~ "deps"
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName, Source = "File", FileName, FolderPath, SHA256, MD5, ProcessCommandLine="", InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine )
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where SHA256 =~ "6144d433f8a0316869877b5f834c801251bbb936e5f1577c5680878c7443c98b"
     or MD5 =~ "42b59fdbe1b72895b2951412222ebf40"
     or TargetProcessName has "src/hooks/deps"
     or ActingProcessName has "src/hooks/deps"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, TargetProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, SHA256, MD5
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Atomic Arch: systemd unit with Restart=always dropped by non-package-manager process AIInstallation Medium
Hunts the persistence step where deps writes a .service unit under /etc/systemd/system/ (root) or ~/.config/systemd/user/ (unprivileged) with ExecStart pointing into /var/lib/ or user-home directories. Filters legit package managers so only payload-driven drops surface. Rationale: Article explicitly names /etc/systemd/system/ (root) and ~/.config/systemd/user/ (user) plus Restart=always — pairing the path with a non-package-manager initiator strips out routine install activity. Cross-checked vs MITRE T1543.002. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1543/002/
ATT&CKT1543.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Ansible/Chef/Puppet config-management runs writing .service units (initiator will be python/ruby/ssh)
  • Custom in-house deployment scripts dropping app systemd units
  • Developer hand-editing a unit under ~/.config/systemd/user/ via vim/nano
  • Container runtimes (podman, docker generate systemd) emitting user units
Suppression filter
| where ActingProcessName !has_any ("ansible","puppet","chef-client","saltstack","podman","docker","cloud-init")
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Read the dropped .service unit's ExecStart path and confirm whether it points under /var/lib/<random-name>/ or a user home dir; resolve the SHA256 of the ExecStart binary. Step 2 (contain): systemctl disable --now the unit (and the per-user unit via the affected user's session bus), quarantine the ExecStart binary, and revoke the user's session/SSH keys. Step 3 (hunt): If hash matches the Atomic Arch deps SHA, treat host as credential-compromised and reimage; sweep fleet for matching unit names and Restart=always under unusual paths.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
| where FileName endswith ".service"
| where FolderPath has_any ("/etc/systemd/system/","/.config/systemd/user/")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("pacman","makepkg","systemctl","systemd-sysv-install","dpkg","apt","apt-get","rpm","dnf","yum","snapd","flatpak")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FolderPath, FileName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessAccountName, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
| where TargetFileName endswith ".service"
| where TargetFilePath has_any ("/etc/systemd/system/","/.config/systemd/user/")
| where not (ActingProcessName has_any ("pacman","makepkg","systemctl","systemd-sysv-install","dpkg","apt","apt-get","rpm","dnf","yum","snapd","flatpak"))
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ActorUsername
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Suspicious systemd .service Drop Outside Package Managers
id: 2b9d4c1e-5a8f-4321-9c7b-3e1d5f6a7b8c
description: Detects creation of systemd .service units by processes other than legitimate Linux package managers, matching Atomic Arch persistence pattern.
references:

Atomic Arch: eBPF rootkit pinned maps hidden_pids/hidden_names/hidden_inodes in /sys/fs/bpf/ AIInstallation High
Direct rootkit IOC — the optional eBPF stage pins three named BPF maps under /sys/fs/bpf/ to hide its processes, names, and socket inodes. Article-specific map names; almost zero benign overlap. Rationale: Three map names are taken verbatim from the article and the Whanos reverse-engineering writeup; /sys/fs/bpf/ pinned maps with these names have no plausible benign explanation. High-fidelity rootkit indicator. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1014/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1564/
ATT&CKT1014 T1564 T1622
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Security researcher loading a benign demo BPF program named identically
  • Detection engineer running this very query's reproducer in a lab
  • BPF observability tooling using overlapping debug names (very unlikely with these specific names)
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): On the host, run bpftool map list and bpftool prog show — capture every pinned map under /sys/fs/bpf/ plus its owning PID and program tag. Step 2 (contain): Treat the host as rootkit-active and disconnect from network. The article is explicit: a package manager cannot prove the system is clean. Step 3 (hunt): Schedule the host for reinstall from trusted media, rotate every credential the user touched (browser sessions, GitHub/npm/Vault tokens, SSH keys, Slack/Teams/Discord, Docker/Podman, VPN), and sweep the fleet for the same map names plus for the deps SHA256.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FolderPath startswith "/sys/fs/bpf/"
| where FileName in~ ("hidden_pids","hidden_names","hidden_inodes")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FolderPath, FileName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessAccountName, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where TargetFilePath startswith "/sys/fs/bpf/"
| where TargetFileName in~ ("hidden_pids","hidden_names","hidden_inodes")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ActorUsername
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Atomic Arch: outbound HTTP upload to temp.sh from developer/build host AIActions on Objectives High
Detects the stealer's exfil channel — credential bundles posted over plain HTTP to temp.sh. Article-specific exfil destination; not a generic dynDNS pattern. Rationale: temp.sh is the exfil destination named by the article and ioctl.fail IOC bundle. Plain HTTP makes this a clean URL/host-match detection on either web-session or DNS telemetry without needing TLS inspection. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1567/002/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1071/001/
ATT&CKT1567.002 T1071.001
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Web.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer legitimately using temp.sh to share a paste/log file with a colleague
  • Helpdesk staff uploading a diagnostic bundle for vendor support
  • CI job using temp.sh as a transient artifact drop
  • Threat researcher reviewing the campaign's exfil endpoint from a sandbox
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("firefox","chrome","chromium","brave","msedge","thunderbird") and InitiatingProcessFolderPath has_any ("/var/lib/","/tmp/","/home/","/.cache/","/.config/")
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Identify the initiating process and folder path — if it's a non-browser, non-curl process running out of /var/lib/, /tmp/, or a user home, treat as confirmed exfil. Pull the host's recent AUR build history. Step 2 (contain): Sinkhole temp.sh at the proxy/firewall (or block-list the resolved IPs), isolate the host, and revoke every developer credential the stealer scope lists (browser, GitHub, npm, Vault, OpenAI, Slack/Teams/Discord, Docker/Podman, SSH). Step 3 (hunt): Pivot on the initiating process binary's SHA256 and check fleet-wide; correlate with the systemd-persistence and BPF-map UCs above to identify other compromised hosts.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where RemoteUrl has "temp.sh" or RemoteUrl endswith ".temp.sh"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemoteUrl, RemotePort, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessSHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImWebSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where HttpHostName endswith "temp.sh" or Url has "temp.sh"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, SrcHostname, SrcUsername, HttpMethod, HttpHostName, Url, HttpRequestBodyBytes, DstIpAddr
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Atomic Arch: non-Tor-aware process connecting to local SOCKS proxy on 9050/9150 AICommand & Control Medium
Hunts the C2 channel — the stealer routes through a localhost Tor SOCKS proxy on 9050/9150. Detection focuses on dev/build hosts where Tor traffic to onion services is not part of the normal workflow. Rationale: Article notes C2 via Tor onion through a local loopback proxy; 9050/9150 are the canonical Tor SOCKS ports. Suppressing the small set of legitimate Tor processes turns this into a high-fidelity dev-host indicator. Sentinel ImNetworkSession lacks process context so we lean on 5-tuple plus a count threshold to bias toward sustained beaconing. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1090/003/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1573/
ATT&CKT1090.003 T1573 T1071.001
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer running torsocks or proxychains for legitimate access to onion services
  • Privacy-conscious user running their own Tor client for personal traffic
  • Researcher analyzing onion infrastructure from a workstation
  • Tails/Whonix-style hardened workstation pattern leaking to corporate telemetry
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Capture the initiating process SHA256 and command line — match against the deps IOC and check FolderPath for /var/lib/, /tmp/, or user-home origin. Confirm tor binary is actually present and running on host. Step 2 (contain): Kill the offending process and its parent systemd unit; block 9050/9150 outbound at host firewall except for sanctioned Tor processes. Step 3 (hunt): Resolve the host's DNS history for the onion bootstrap domains (consensus directory authorities, *.torproject.org), correlate with the temp.sh exfil UC, and pivot to other dev hosts on the same subnet with loopback Tor connections.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Loopback" or RemoteIP in ("127.0.0.1","::1")
| where RemotePort in (9050, 9150)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("tor","torbrowser-launcher","firefox","firefox-esr","brave","obfs4proxy","snowflake-client")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessSHA256, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| order by Timestamp desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where DstIpAddr in ("127.0.0.1","::1")
| where DstPortNumber in (9050, 9150)
| summarize ConnCount = count(), FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated) by DvcHostname, SrcUsername, SrcIpAddr, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount >= 3
| order by LastSeen desc
title: Non-Tor Process Connecting to Local SOCKS Proxy 9050 or 9150
id: 7a2c5d9e-3b4f-4108-9d2e-5f6a7b8c9d0e
description: Detects processes other than Tor itself or Tor-aware browsers connecting to the local Tor SOCKS proxy ports — matching Atomic Arch C2 routing.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/over-400-arch-linux-aur-packages.html
author: Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/12
tags:
  - attack.command_and_control
  - attack.t1090.003
  - attack.t1573
logsource:
  category: network_connection
  product: linux
detection:
  selection:
    DestinationIp:
      - '127.0.0.1'
      - '::1'
    DestinationPort:
      - 9050
      - 9150
  filter_tor:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/tor'
      - '/firefox'
      - '/firefox-esr'
      - '/brave'
      - '/torbrowser-launcher'
      - '/obfs4proxy'
  condition: selection and not filter_tor
level: medium
source:linux.auditd (@network.destination.ip:(127.0.0.1 OR ::1)) (@network.destination.port:9050 OR @network.destination.port:9150) -@process.name:(tor OR firefox OR firefox-esr OR brave OR torbrowser-launcher OR obfs4proxy OR snowflake-client)
#event_simpleName=NetworkConnectIP4
| RemoteAddressIP4="127.0.0.1"
| RemotePort=9050 OR RemotePort=9150
| NOT regex("(tor|firefox|firefox-esr|brave|torbrowser-launcher|obfs4proxy|snowflake-client)$", field=ContextImageFileName)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, RemotePort], function=count())
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(All_Traffic.process_name) as process_name values(All_Traffic.user) as user from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic where All_Traffic.dest IN ("127.0.0.1","::1") AND All_Traffic.dest_port IN (9050,9150) AND NOT All_Traffic.process_name IN ("tor","firefox","torbrowser-launcher","brave","obfs4proxy","snowflake-client") by All_Traffic.src All_Traffic.process_name All_Traffic.dest_port | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)` | sort - lastTime
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(All_Traffic.process_name) as process_name values(All_Traffic.user) as user from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic where All_Traffic.dest IN ("127.0.0.1","::1") AND All_Traffic.dest_port IN (9050,9150) AND NOT All_Traffic.process_name IN ("tor","firefox","torbrowser-launcher","brave","obfs4proxy","snowflake-client") by All_Traffic.src All_Traffic.process_name All_Traffic.dest_port | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)` | sort - lastTime
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
Network connections to article IPs / domains Command & Control High
Outbound traffic to attacker infrastructure named in the article.
ATT&CKT1071
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Web Network_Resolution.DNS DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteIP in ("") or RemoteUrl has_any ("olrh4mibs62l6kkuvvjyc5lrercqg5tz543r4lsw3o6mh5qb7g7sneid.onion", "temp.sh")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
let BadIPs     = dynamic([""]);
let BadDomains = dynamic(["olrh4mibs62l6kkuvvjyc5lrercqg5tz543r4lsw3o6mh5qb7g7sneid.onion", "temp.sh"]);
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where DstIpAddr in (BadIPs)
   or Url has_any (BadDomains)
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, Url, NetworkProtocol
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs Actions on Objectives High
Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies SQLite from Chrome/Edge/Firefox.
ATT&CKT1539 T1555.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\", @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\", @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where FileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FolderPath, FileName, ActionType

// ASIM ImFileEvent — covers MDE, Sysmon, AuditD, Defender for Cloud, etc.
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\",
                                  @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\",
                                  @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where TargetFileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where ActingProcessName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
