title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
Microsoft Teams external-tenant chat from unverified IT-helpdesk impersonator Delivery High
External Teams chat where displayName contains 'helpdesk' or 'IT support' — common 2024+ vishing pattern (Storm-1811, Black Basta, UNC6692). No CIM data model maps to Teams chats; uses raw O365 audit logs.
ATT&CKT1566.004 T1566
Data sourcesCloudAppEvents
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where Application == "Microsoft Teams"
| where ActionType == "MessageSent"
| where RawEventData has "ExternalParticipants"
| extend SenderDisplayName = tostring(parse_json(RawEventData).SenderDisplayName)
| where SenderDisplayName matches regex @"(?i)(help.?desk|it.?support|service.?desk|tech.?support|admin)"
| project Timestamp, AccountDisplayName, IPAddress, ActivityType, SenderDisplayName, RawEventData
// External Teams chat — Teams audit lives in OfficeActivity.
OfficeActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OfficeWorkload == "MicrosoftTeams"
| where Operation in~ ("MessageSent","ChatCreated","TeamsImpersonationDetected")
| where isnotempty(UserId)
| where Subject has_any ("IT","helpdesk","support","password","verify")
   or Recipients has_any ("IT","helpdesk")
| project TimeGenerated, UserId, Operation, Subject, Recipients,
          ClientIP, UserAgent
| order by TimeGenerated desc
CLOUD
`o365_management_activity`
  Workload=MicrosoftTeams Operation=MessageSent
  ExternalParticipants=*
| where match(SenderDisplayName, "(?i)(help.?desk|it.?support|service.?desk|tech.?support|admin)")
| stats count, earliest(_time) as firstTime, latest(_time) as lastTime
    by SenderUpn, SenderDisplayName, RecipientUpn, ChatId
RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard Installation High
ConnectWise / AnyDesk / TeamViewer / ScreenConnect / Atera installed outside IT change windows = common tradecraft for ransomware affiliates and IT-helpdesk impersonators.
ATT&CKT1219
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("AnyDesk.exe","TeamViewer.exe","TeamViewer_Service.exe",
        "ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe","ConnectWiseControl.ClientService.exe",
        "atera_agent.exe","SplashtopStreamer.exe","RustDesk.exe","NinjaOne.exe")
   or FileName matches regex @"(?i)kaseya.*\.exe"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\AnyDesk.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\TeamViewer.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\TeamViewer_Service.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\ConnectWiseControl.ClientService.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\atera_agent.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\SplashtopStreamer.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\RustDesk.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\NinjaOne.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName,
          CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Remote-Management (RMM) Tool Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d0c
status: experimental
description: |
    AnyDesk / TeamViewer / ScreenConnect / Atera / Splashtop /
    RustDesk — RMM tools attackers commonly install for hands-on-
    keyboard access. Filter against the IT estate's known tool.
references:

    category: process_creation

detection:

            - '\AnyDesk.exe'

Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("AnyDesk.exe","TeamViewer.exe","TeamViewer_Service.exe",
        "ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe","ConnectWiseControl.ClientService.exe",
        "atera_agent.exe","SplashtopStreamer.exe","RustDesk.exe","NinjaOne.exe","kaseya*.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("AnyDesk.exe","TeamViewer.exe","TeamViewer_Service.exe",
        "ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe","ConnectWiseControl.ClientService.exe",
        "atera_agent.exe","SplashtopStreamer.exe","RustDesk.exe","NinjaOne.exe","kaseya*.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
OAuth consent / suspicious app grant Actions on Objectives High
Cloud identity abuse: app gets high-priv scopes, often via consent phishing.
ATT&CKT1528 T1098.001
Data sourcesAuthentication.Authentication CloudAppEvents
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("Consent to application.","Add OAuth2PermissionGrant.","Add delegated permission grant.")
| project Timestamp, AccountObjectId, AccountDisplayName, ActivityType,
          ActivityObjects, IPAddress, UserAgent
// Entra ID directory audit — user / admin consent to a third-party app.
AuditLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OperationName has "Consent to application"
| where Result =~ "success"
| extend AppName = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].displayName),

         User    = tostring(parse_json(tostring(InitiatedBy)).user.userPrincipalName)

| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc

| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`

title: FakeCaptcha / ClickFix - Clipboard-Injected PowerShell from Explorer
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d06
status: experimental
description: |

    user to press Win+R and paste a payload. The result is
    powershell/mshta launched directly from explorer.exe with iex /
    base64 / downloadstring in the command line.

    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1204/002/

    category: process_creation
    product: windows

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("6144d433f8a0316869877b5f834c801251bbb936e5f1577c5680878c7443c98b", "42b59fdbe1b72895b2951412222ebf40") or SHA1 in~ ("6144d433f8a0316869877b5f834c801251bbb936e5f1577c5680878c7443c98b", "42b59fdbe1b72895b2951412222ebf40") or MD5 in~ ("6144d433f8a0316869877b5f834c801251bbb936e5f1577c5680878c7443c98b", "42b59fdbe1b72895b2951412222ebf40")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("6144d433f8a0316869877b5f834c801251bbb936e5f1577c5680878c7443c98b", "42b59fdbe1b72895b2951412222ebf40") or SHA1 in~ ("6144d433f8a0316869877b5f834c801251bbb936e5f1577c5680878c7443c98b", "42b59fdbe1b72895b2951412222ebf40") or MD5 in~ ("6144d433f8a0316869877b5f834c801251bbb936e5f1577c5680878c7443c98b", "42b59fdbe1b72895b2951412222ebf40")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["6144d433f8a0316869877b5f834c801251bbb936e5f1577c5680878c7443c98b", "42b59fdbe1b72895b2951412222ebf40"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process · Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key.
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → OAuth consent / suspicious app grant
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest

| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`

| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user
| join type=inner user
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
        from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
     | rename Processes.user as user]
| tstats summariesonly=false count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user
| join type=inner user
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
        from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
     | rename Processes.user as user]

| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
SecurityEvent

title: Office Application Spawning Script Host
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d07
status: experimental
description: |
    Word/Excel/Outlook/OneNote spawning powershell, cmd, wscript,
    cscript, mshta, rundll32, regsvr32 — classic macro / embedded-
    object payload signature.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1566/001/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059
    - attack.t1566.001
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_parent:
        ParentImage|endswith:
            - '\winword.exe'
            - '\excel.exe'
            - '\powerpnt.exe'
            - '\outlook.exe'
            - '\onenote.exe'
            - '\mspub.exe'
            - '\visio.exe'
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
    condition: selection_parent and selection_child
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate automation macros in trusted internal documents
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe","outlook.exe","onenote.exe","mspub.exe","visio.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe","outlook.exe","onenote.exe","mspub.exe","visio.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
OAuth consent / suspicious app grant Actions on Objectives High
Cloud identity abuse: app gets high-priv scopes, often via consent phishing.
ATT&CKT1528 T1098.001
Data sourcesAuthentication.Authentication CloudAppEvents
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("Consent to application.","Add OAuth2PermissionGrant.","Add delegated permission grant.")
| project Timestamp, AccountObjectId, AccountDisplayName, ActivityType,
          ActivityObjects, IPAddress, UserAgent
// Entra ID directory audit — user / admin consent to a third-party app.
AuditLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OperationName has "Consent to application"
| where Result =~ "success"
| extend AppName = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].displayName),
         AppId   = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].id),
         User    = tostring(parse_json(tostring(InitiatedBy)).user.userPrincipalName)
| project TimeGenerated, OperationName, User, AppName, AppId, Result
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) Exploitation High
Browser-pasted PowerShell launched from explorer/Run dialog — ClickFix social engineering.
ATT&CKT1204.004 T1059.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("explorer.exe","RuntimeBroker.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(iex|invoke-expression|frombase64|downloadstring|hxxp|curl |wget )"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName endswith "\explorer.exe"
   or ParentProcessName endswith "\RuntimeBroker.exe"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\pwsh.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| where CommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(iex|invoke-expression|frombase64|downloadstring|hxxp|curl |wget )"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: FakeCaptcha / ClickFix - Clipboard-Injected PowerShell from Explorer
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d06
status: experimental
description: |
    "FakeCaptcha" / "ClickFix" social-engineering: malicious site asks
    user to press Win+R and paste a payload. The result is
    powershell/mshta launched directly from explorer.exe with iex /
    base64 / downloadstring in the command line.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1204/002/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059.001
    - attack.t1204.002
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_parent:
        ParentImage|endswith:
            - '\explorer.exe'
            - '\RuntimeBroker.exe'
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
    selection_cmd:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - 'iex'
            - 'invoke-expression'
            - 'frombase64'
            - 'downloadstring'
            - 'hxxp'
            - 'curl '
            - 'wget '
    condition: selection_parent and selection_child and selection_cmd
falsepositives:
    - IT-driven scripted automation that admins paste-launch
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("explorer.exe","RuntimeBroker.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*iex*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*hxxp*" OR Processes.process="*curl*" OR Processes.process="*wget*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("explorer.exe","RuntimeBroker.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*iex*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*hxxp*" OR Processes.process="*curl*" OR Processes.process="*wget*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children Exploitation Medium
Supply-chain trojan signal: legitimate signed binary spawning script interpreters or exotic LOLBins.
ATT&CKT1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
// Replace `"setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe"` with the vendor binaries observed in the
// article (matching shape with the Defender query).
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\bitsadmin.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Trusted Vendor Binary Launching Unusual Children
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d09
status: experimental
description: |
    A signed vendor binary (in the article's named-vendors list)
    spawning script-host or LOLBin children. Strongest signal when
    paired with a recent CVE / supply-chain advisory naming the same
    vendor.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1195
    - attack.initial-access
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\wmic.exe'
            - '\bitsadmin.exe'
    selection_parent_vendor:
        ParentImage|contains:
            - '\Program Files\'
            - '\Program Files (x86)\'
    condition: selection_child and selection_parent_vendor
falsepositives:
    - Many — installers and updaters legitimately spawn children. Pin
      the parent path to specific vendor binaries observed in the
      article before alerting.
level: medium

      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process

Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-21509", "CVE-2023-50224")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-21509", "CVE-2023-50224")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

Budibase /api/public/v1/roles/assign POST exploitation (CVE-2026-48150) AIExploitation High
Hunts successful POSTs to the vulnerable Budibase public API roles-assignment endpoint, optionally scoped by the x-budibase-app-id / x-budibase-api-key headers from the PoC. On affected versions (<3.39.0) any workspace-scoped builder can call this endpoint and grant builder.global / admin.global, so every successful hit is a privilege-escalation candidate. Rationale: Anchored on the exact vulnerable route `/api/public/v1/roles/assign` named at packages/server/src/api/controllers/public/roles.ts:13-17 and the PoC `curl -X POST` from the advisory. Restricted to 2xx responses because the SDK only writes builder.global / admin.global on a successful userDB.bulkUpdate, so 4xx noise is filtered out at the query layer.
ATT&CKT1190 T1068
Data sourcesWeb
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate Enterprise tenant admin creating new global builders/admins via the public API after a license-feature rollout
  • Budibase platform/SRE smoke-test scripts that POST to the endpoint as part of release validation
  • IaC / Terraform provider for Budibase reconciling role assignments at scheduled intervals
  • Pen-test or internal red-team exercise from a known engagement source IP
Suppression filter
| where not (SrcIpAddr in ("<admin_jumphost_ip_1>","<admin_jumphost_ip_2>") and HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent has_any ("BudibaseAdminCLI","Terraform/budibase-provider"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the source IP and any x-budibase-api-key header value from the access log, resolve the API key to its owning user via Budibase admin console, and confirm whether that user holds builder.global=true OR admin.global=true PRIOR to the request (workspace-scoped callers are the exploit primitive). 2) Contain: rotate the implicated API key, revoke the user's session, downgrade builder/admin flags on any user whose state changed in the same time window, and (if running <3.39.0) hotfix to 3.39.0 or apply the reverse-proxy block on the route until patched. 3) Hunt: pivot on the source IP and API key for any other /api/public/v1/* calls in the prior 24h; enumerate every user whose builder.global or admin.global flipped to true in the same window; review datasource-credential and SCIM/OIDC config reads following the escalation.
ImWebSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where HttpMethod =~ "POST"
| where Url has "/api/public/v1/roles/assign"
| where HttpStatusCode in ("200","201")
| extend AppIdHeader = extract(@"(?i)x-budibase-app-id:\s*(app_[A-Za-z0-9]+)", 1, tostring(HttpRequestHeaderCookie))
| project TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername, DstHostname, Url, HttpMethod, HttpStatusCode, HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent, AppIdHeader, EventVendor, EventProduct
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Budibase CVE-2026-48150 PoC chain: self API key mint then roles/assign within 5 min AIExploitation High
Detects the exact two-step exploitation sequence from the advisory: a GET to /api/global/self/api_key (Alice mints an API key tied to her workspace-scoped identity) immediately followed by a POST to /api/public/v1/roles/assign from the same source IP / user. The temporal proximity of these endpoints is the strongest article-specific signal. Rationale: Two endpoint strings from the PoC walkthrough (Step 2 `GET /api/global/self/api_key` and Step 3 `POST /api/public/v1/roles/assign`) executed back-to-back from the same caller. The advisory shows these requests are seconds apart in the attacker's curl sequence; a 5-minute join window is generous enough to catch human-paced exploitation while still being well below the noise floor of independent endpoint use.
ATT&CKT1098 T1068 T1078.004
Data sourcesWeb
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • A platform admin rotating their own API key and then immediately granting a new global builder role to onboard a colleague (rare but legitimate)
  • Automation / IaC pipeline that programmatically mints an API key then provisions roles
  • QA / staging tenant where engineers regularly exercise both endpoints back-to-back
  • Budibase platform self-test or release smoke test that exercises the public API end-to-end
Suppression filter
| where SrcUsername !in ("budibase-platform-admin", "svc-budibase-iac") and HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent !has "BudibaseDeployer"
Response runbook
1) Triage: identify the user behind both requests via the x-budibase-api-key header → user lookup; pull their builder.apps / builder.global / admin.global state at T-1 and T+0. If T-1 shows builder.apps populated with builder.global=false and T+0 shows builder.global=true (or admin.global=true), this is exploitation. 2) Contain: revoke the freshly minted API key, force-logout the user, restore builder/admin flags on any users whose state changed in the surrounding window, and block the source IP at the WAF if external. 3) Hunt: pull every /api/public/v1/* and /api/global/* call from the same SrcIpAddr or API key over the last 7 days; review audit logs for SCIM, OIDC, automation, and datasource credential reads after the assign event; check for additional impersonation chains (assign-builder, then call as builder, then assign-admin).
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let WindowSeconds = 300;
let ApiKeyMints = ImWebSession
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where HttpMethod =~ "GET"
    | where Url has "/api/global/self/api_key"
    | where HttpStatusCode in ("200","201")
    | project KeyMintTime = TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername, DstHostname;
ImWebSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where HttpMethod =~ "POST"
| where Url has "/api/public/v1/roles/assign"
| where HttpStatusCode in ("200","201")
| join kind=inner ApiKeyMints on SrcIpAddr
| where TimeGenerated between (KeyMintTime .. KeyMintTime + WindowSeconds * 1s)
| extend DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', TimeGenerated, KeyMintTime)
| project KeyMintTime, AssignTime = TimeGenerated, DelaySec, SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername, DstHostname, Url, HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent
| order by AssignTime desc
source:(nginx OR apache.access OR http OR aws.alb OR azure.appservice) (@http.url_details.path:*/api/global/self/api_key* OR @http.url_details.path:*/api/public/v1/roles/assign*) @http.status_code:(200 OR 201)
# log group: /aws/elasticloadbalancing/<alb-name>
fields @timestamp, client_ip, request_verb, request_url, elb_status_code, user_agent
| filter (request_url like /\/api\/global\/self\/api_key/ or request_url like /\/api\/public\/v1\/roles\/assign/)
      and elb_status_code in [200, 201]
| stats earliest(@timestamp) as keymint_ts by client_ip, request_url
| sort keymint_ts desc
| limit 500

Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` min(_time) as keymint_time from datamodel=Web where Web.http_method=GET Web.url="*/api/global/self/api_key*" Web.status IN (200,201) by Web.src Web.user | rename Web.src as src Web.user as user | join type=inner src [ | tstats `summariesonly` min(_time) as assign_time from datamodel=Web where Web.http_method=POST Web.url="*/api/public/v1/roles/assign*" Web.status IN (200,201) by Web.src Web.user | rename Web.src as src Web.user as user_assign ] | where assign_time >= keymint_time AND (assign_time - keymint_time) <= 300 | eval delay_sec = assign_time - keymint_time | eval cve="CVE-2026-48150" | convert ctime(keymint_time) ctime(assign_time) | table keymint_time, assign_time, delay_sec, src, user, user_assign | sort - assign_time
| tstats summariesonly=false min(_time) as keymint_time from datamodel=Web where Web.http_method=GET Web.url="*/api/global/self/api_key*" Web.status IN (200,201) by Web.src Web.user | rename Web.src as src Web.user as user | join type=inner src [ | tstats summariesonly=false min(_time) as assign_time from datamodel=Web where Web.http_method=POST Web.url="*/api/public/v1/roles/assign*" Web.status IN (200,201) by Web.src Web.user | rename Web.src as src Web.user as user_assign ] | where assign_time >= keymint_time AND (assign_time - keymint_time) <= 300 | eval delay_sec = assign_time - keymint_time | eval cve="CVE-2026-48150" | convert ctime(keymint_time) ctime(assign_time) | table keymint_time, assign_time, delay_sec, src, user, user_assign | sort - assign_time
Budibase bulk role-assign requests from single source (CVE-2026-48150 mass-promotion) AIExploitation Medium
Detects burst exploitation where one source IP or API key issues multiple successful POSTs to /api/public/v1/roles/assign in a short window — the article's impact section notes the SDK overwrite strips existing builder.apps scoping, so attackers iterate to promote both themselves and other users (builder, then admin, then victim accounts). Rationale: Article impact section: 'the mass-assignment also strips scoping from the target's existing role, so downgrading a legitimate global builder to an app-scoped builder fails: a later call reinstates global: true.' Combined with the PoC showing the attacker chains separate calls (Step 3 grants builder, Step 4 grants admin), >3 successful POSTs per 5-min bucket from one source is the signature of either tooling-driven mass promotion or repeated escalation attempts.
ATT&CKT1068 T1098
Data sourcesWeb
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Initial tenant bootstrap where an admin uses a script to provision dozens of builder users in one go
  • Migration of users from one identity provider to another that involves bulk role-assign calls
  • Budibase platform-team load test against a staging instance
  • Backup/restore tooling that re-applies role assignments after a tenant restore
Suppression filter
| where SrcIpAddr !in ("<known_admin_jumphost>","<budibase_iac_runner>") and not (HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent has_any ("Terraform","BudibaseAdminCLI","BudibaseBootstrap"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the SrcIpAddr / API key owner and enumerate the userIds passed in each POST body (request body logging if enabled, else infer from the audit-log user-state changes). Confirm whether the API-key owner held admin.global=true at T-1 — if not, this is exploitation. 2) Contain: invalidate the API key, revoke sessions for every user whose builder.global or admin.global flipped to true in the burst window, and put the /api/public/v1/roles/assign route behind a temporary WAF block until the tenant is patched to 3.39.0+. 3) Hunt: review all datasource-credential reads, SCIM / OIDC config changes, automation runs, and outbound webhook destinations from any newly-promoted account in the following 24h; check for newly minted API keys via /api/global/self/api_key for each promoted user (the attacker may have minted keys for victim accounts to maintain access).
ImWebSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where HttpMethod =~ "POST"
| where Url has "/api/public/v1/roles/assign"
| where HttpStatusCode in ("200","201")
| summarize AssignCount = count(),
            FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated),
            LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated),
            UserAgents = make_set(HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent, 5),
            DstHosts = make_set(DstHostname, 5)
            by SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername, bin(TimeGenerated, 5m)
| where AssignCount > 3   // empirical: legitimate admin promotions are sporadic, not bursty
| order by AssignCount desc, LastSeen desc
source:(nginx OR apache.access OR http OR aws.alb OR azure.appservice) @http.method:POST @http.url_details.path:*/api/public/v1/roles/assign* @http.status_code:(200 OR 201)
# log group: /aws/elasticloadbalancing/<alb-name>
fields @timestamp, client_ip, request_verb, request_url, elb_status_code, user_agent
| filter request_verb = "POST"
      and request_url like /\/api\/public\/v1\/roles\/assign/
      and elb_status_code in [200, 201]
| stats count(*) as assign_count, earliest(@timestamp) as first_seen, latest(@timestamp) as last_seen by client_ip, bin(5m)
| filter assign_count > 3
| sort assign_count desc

China-Linked Hackers Backdoored Linux Login Software to Hide for Nearly a Decade

The Hacker News
2026-06-12 12 use cases 4 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

Instead of hiding on the laptops and servers defenders watch most closely, a China-nexus group spent close to a decade hidden inside the Linux login system itself. Sygnia, which tracks the group as Velvet Ant, says it backdoored the PAM and OpenSSH components that decide who is allowed to sign in, planting its access where ordinary cleanup could not reach it. The network it targeted had no

Velvet Ant backdoored PAM authentication module replacement on Linux AIInstallation High
Hunts for write/replace events targeting PAM security modules on Linux endpoints (libpam, pam_unix.so, pam_*.so). Sygnia found nine separate backdoored PAM variants planted by Velvet Ant under /lib/security/, /lib64/security/ and /lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/security/ that either accept a secret password or silently log real credentials. Rationale: Article: 'On many machines, the attacker replaced the main PAM login module with backdoored copies' and 'Researchers found nine separate versions.' Detection pivots on writes to canonical PAM library locations by non-package-manager processes — the package-manager exclusion strips the only normal source of changes to these files. Cross-checked with Sygnia 2024 reporting on Velvet Ant and MITRE T1556.003. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1556/003/ • https://www.sygnia.co/blog/
ATT&CKT1556.003 T1556 T1554
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem_Changes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Distro security update via dpkg/rpm patching libpam (filtered by package-manager exclusion)
  • Configuration management (Ansible/Puppet/Chef) pushing PAM module updates from a deploy account
  • Admin manually rebuilding a custom PAM module after kernel upgrade
  • SSSD or winbind package upgrade replacing pam_sss.so / pam_winbind.so
  • Container image bake rebuilding /lib/security/ inside a chroot/overlayfs
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("dpkg","rpm","yum","dnf","apt","apt-get","zypper","pacman","unattended-upgrade","update-alternatives")
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !in~ ("ansible","puppet","salt","chef")
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: hash the modified PAM library on disk and compare to the same package version's checksum from the distro repo (`dpkg --verify libpam-modules` / `rpm -V pam`). If the file is unsigned or hash mismatches, escalate. Capture `lsof` of sshd and any running shells using the library. Step 2 — Contain: isolate the host from the management network (do NOT reboot — backdoored login may persist across reboot and you lose volatile evidence). Force-restore the PAM module from a known-good package via `apt --reinstall install libpam-modules` from a trusted mirror after taking a memory image. Step 3 — Hunt: pivot on the writing process's parent chain, search for the same SHA256 across the fleet, and check for OpenSSH binary tampering (UC 'OpenSSH sshd binary tampering') — Velvet Ant pairs PAM and SSH backdoors.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where DeviceCategory_Or_OSPlatform_proxy == DeviceCategory_Or_OSPlatform_proxy // keep placeholder readable
| where FolderPath has_any (@"/lib/security/", @"/lib64/security/", @"/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/security/", @"/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/security/", @"/lib/aarch64-linux-gnu/security/")
   or FileName in~ ("pam_unix.so","pam_sss.so","pam_winbind.so","pam_tally2.so","pam_cracklib.so","pam_systemd.so","libpam.so.0","libpam_misc.so.0")
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("dpkg","rpm","yum","dnf","apt","apt-get","zypper","pacman","unattended-upgrade","update-alternatives")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FolderPath, FileName, SHA256, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"/lib/security/", @"/lib64/security/", @"/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/security/", @"/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/security/", @"/lib/aarch64-linux-gnu/security/")
   or TargetFileName in~ ("pam_unix.so","pam_sss.so","pam_winbind.so","pam_tally2.so","pam_cracklib.so","pam_systemd.so","libpam.so.0","libpam_misc.so.0")
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where ActingProcessName !in~ ("dpkg","rpm","yum","dnf","apt","apt-get","zypper","pacman","unattended-upgrade","update-alternatives")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, TargetFileSHA256, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ActorUsername
| order by TimeGenerated desc

OpenSSH sshd/ssh binary tampering on Linux (Velvet Ant Operation Highland) AIInstallation High
Detects modification or replacement of the OpenSSH daemon and client binaries. Sygnia reports Velvet Ant altered /usr/sbin/sshd and /usr/bin/ssh to log every credential typed and every command issued, with a hidden runtime switch to disable the logger. Watches writes to the binaries themselves rather than to their config. Rationale: Article: 'The OpenSSH programs were altered the same way, logging credentials and every command typed, with a hidden switch to turn that logging off when needed.' Detection pins on writes to the canonical sshd/ssh paths by non-packager processes — file integrity is the article's recommended verification approach ('compare these programs against known-good copies'). Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1554/ • https://www.sygnia.co/blog/
ATT&CKT1554 T1556
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem_Changes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • openssh-server distro security update via apt/dnf (filtered)
  • Custom in-house sshd build deployed via configuration management
  • Snap/flatpak/portable OpenSSH refresh in /usr/lib/snapd/snap/openssh-server
  • Container image rebuild copying a new sshd into /usr/sbin via overlayfs
  • Hardening tool (e.g. Lynis, OpenSCAP) reapplying ownership/SELinux context (modifies inode metadata, not contents — exclude by ActionType if needed)
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("dpkg","rpm","yum","dnf","apt","apt-get","zypper","pacman","unattended-upgrade","snapd")
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath !startswith "/snap/"
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: hash /usr/sbin/sshd and compare to the openssh-server package's expected hash (`dpkg --verify openssh-server` / `rpm -V openssh-server`). Diff against a known-good binary from the same distro/version on an air-gapped reference. Step 2 — Contain: do NOT restart sshd until you have a memory image — the backdoor may carry an in-memory toggle. Block inbound 22/tcp from non-jump-host sources at the network edge. Step 3 — Hunt: search for the same write SHA256 across the fleet (Velvet Ant deployed nine PAM variants — expect multiple sshd variants too). Pull /var/log/auth.log for the prior 90 days looking for logins that succeeded without a corresponding PAM acct_mgmt entry — indicator of the backdoor's secret-password path.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FolderPath in~ ("/usr/sbin/", "/usr/bin/", "/usr/lib/openssh/", "/usr/libexec/openssh/")
| where FileName in~ ("sshd","ssh","scp","sftp","sftp-server","ssh-keygen","ssh-agent")
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("dpkg","rpm","yum","dnf","apt","apt-get","zypper","pacman","unattended-upgrade")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FolderPath, FileName, SHA256, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where TargetFilePath in~ ("/usr/sbin/sshd","/usr/bin/ssh","/usr/bin/scp","/usr/bin/sftp","/usr/lib/openssh/sftp-server","/usr/libexec/openssh/sftp-server","/usr/bin/ssh-keygen","/usr/bin/ssh-agent")
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where ActingProcessName !in~ ("dpkg","rpm","yum","dnf","apt","apt-get","zypper","pacman","unattended-upgrade")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ActorUsername
| order by TimeGenerated desc

sshd writing non-standard files — credential capture sink indicator AIActions on Objectives Medium
Hunts for the sshd process writing files to anything other than its expected runtime paths (sshd_config, host keys, utmp/wtmp, /var/log/auth.log via syslog). Sygnia reports the backdoored OpenSSH 'logging credentials and every command typed' — that log has to land somewhere on disk, and a hidden cache file written by sshd itself is the cleanest tell. Rationale: Article: 'logging credentials and every command typed' implies sshd is writing capture data somewhere outside its normal runtime footprint. Exclusion list covers every legitimate sshd write target (pid files, /etc/ssh keys, user .ssh dirs, syslog spool, sss cache). Anything left is highly suspicious. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1056/001/
ATT&CKT1056.001 T1005 T1556.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem_Changes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Custom session-recording build of sshd writing to /var/sshlog/
  • SELinux/AppArmor denial logs being redirected
  • Admin running `chroot` enabled sshd with non-standard ChrootDirectory writes
  • HPC/cluster build placing sshd PID files outside /var/run
  • Sandbox/dev environment where sshd dumps debug to /tmp
Suppression filter
| where not (FolderPath startswith "/var/sshlog/" or FolderPath startswith "/var/sandbox/")
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: cat the unexpected file. Captured passwords typically appear as `user:plaintext` pairs, captured commands as readable shell strings. Run `strings` on the file and check `lsof -p <sshd_pid>` to confirm sshd has the handle open. Step 2 — Contain: snapshot the file (it's evidence and may be small), then take a memory image of sshd. Block egress from the host pending review — backdoor likely exfiltrates the cache periodically. Step 3 — Hunt: search for any process reading the cache file (`auditctl -w` retroactively or DeviceFileEvents with FileName == capture file) — that's the exfil channel. Cross-check against the PAM module UC: a host with both signals is a confirmed Velvet Ant install.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "sshd"
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
| where not (FolderPath startswith "/var/run/" or FolderPath startswith "/run/" or FolderPath startswith "/var/log/" or FolderPath startswith "/var/lib/sss/" or FolderPath startswith "/tmp/ssh-" or FolderPath startswith "/etc/ssh/" or FolderPath matches regex @"^/home/[^/]+/\.ssh/" or FolderPath startswith "/root/.ssh/" or FolderPath startswith "/proc/")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FolderPath, FileName, FileSize, InitiatingProcessId, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| summarize WriteCount = count(), SamplePath = any(FolderPath), Files = make_set(FileName, 10) by DeviceName, bin(Timestamp, 1h)
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActingProcessName =~ "sshd"
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
| where not (TargetFilePath startswith "/var/run/" or TargetFilePath startswith "/run/" or TargetFilePath startswith "/var/log/" or TargetFilePath startswith "/var/lib/sss/" or TargetFilePath startswith "/tmp/ssh-" or TargetFilePath startswith "/etc/ssh/" or TargetFilePath matches regex @"^/home/[^/]+/\.ssh/" or TargetFilePath startswith "/root/.ssh/" or TargetFilePath startswith "/proc/")
| summarize WriteCount = count(), SamplePath = any(TargetFilePath), Files = make_set(TargetFileName, 10) by DvcHostname, bin(TimeGenerated, 1h)
| order by TimeGenerated desc
source:linux.auditd @auditd.type:PATH @process.name:sshd -@file.path:("/var/run/*" OR "/run/*" OR "/var/log/*" OR "/tmp/ssh-*" OR "/etc/ssh/*" OR "/home/*/.ssh/*" OR "/root/.ssh/*" OR "/var/lib/sss/*" OR "/proc/*")
#event_simpleName=FileWritten ContextImageFileName=/\/sshd$/i
| NOT regex("^/(var/run/|run/|var/log/|var/lib/sss/|tmp/ssh-|tmp/sshd|etc/ssh/|home/[^/]+/\.ssh/|root/\.ssh/|proc/)", field=TargetFileName)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, TargetFileName], function=count())
| count > 0
ENDPOINT
