| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Outbound Connection to Article-Named IP / Domain
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d0f
status: experimental
description: |
    Replace `__IP_LIST__` / `__DOMAIN_LIST__` placeholders with
    article-specific destinations. For dynamic IOC management, use a
    watchlist or external feed.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/tactics/TA0011/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.command-and-control
logsource:
    category: network_connection
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_ip:
        DestinationIp:
            - '__IP_PLACEHOLDER_1__'
            - '__IP_PLACEHOLDER_2__'
    selection_domain:
        DestinationHostname:
            - '__DOMAIN_PLACEHOLDER_1__'
            - '__DOMAIN_PLACEHOLDER_2__'
    condition: selection_ip or selection_domain
falsepositives:
    - None on a true-positive IOC match
level: critical
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.dest IN ("104.18.20.213", "104.21.46.39", "172.67.223.39")
    by All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest, All_Traffic.dest_port
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| append
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count from datamodel=Web
        where Web.dest IN ("akmuniverstall.top")
        by Web.src, Web.dest, Web.url, Web.user

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("41999a3d0da035ff8068905c90235ea50121329cb0661e38d745974ebf5e3ae2", "78945c844fc23dd3446cf17987edeeb6cc21986820c92df82a126af24a5a38d1", "d89bb4b23a67814ef511e4e9dda7ad36fa519a322fa7c25ea451c7dd7ef61e54", "f6e4b09ef788adef3f65fd2b99da8f5be5391be29471676dc07040a56c8fdfab") or SHA1 in~ ("41999a3d0da035ff8068905c90235ea50121329cb0661e38d745974ebf5e3ae2", "78945c844fc23dd3446cf17987edeeb6cc21986820c92df82a126af24a5a38d1", "d89bb4b23a67814ef511e4e9dda7ad36fa519a322fa7c25ea451c7dd7ef61e54", "f6e4b09ef788adef3f65fd2b99da8f5be5391be29471676dc07040a56c8fdfab") or MD5 in~ ("41999a3d0da035ff8068905c90235ea50121329cb0661e38d745974ebf5e3ae2", "78945c844fc23dd3446cf17987edeeb6cc21986820c92df82a126af24a5a38d1", "d89bb4b23a67814ef511e4e9dda7ad36fa519a322fa7c25ea451c7dd7ef61e54", "f6e4b09ef788adef3f65fd2b99da8f5be5391be29471676dc07040a56c8fdfab")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("41999a3d0da035ff8068905c90235ea50121329cb0661e38d745974ebf5e3ae2", "78945c844fc23dd3446cf17987edeeb6cc21986820c92df82a126af24a5a38d1", "d89bb4b23a67814ef511e4e9dda7ad36fa519a322fa7c25ea451c7dd7ef61e54", "f6e4b09ef788adef3f65fd2b99da8f5be5391be29471676dc07040a56c8fdfab") or SHA1 in~ ("41999a3d0da035ff8068905c90235ea50121329cb0661e38d745974ebf5e3ae2", "78945c844fc23dd3446cf17987edeeb6cc21986820c92df82a126af24a5a38d1", "d89bb4b23a67814ef511e4e9dda7ad36fa519a322fa7c25ea451c7dd7ef61e54", "f6e4b09ef788adef3f65fd2b99da8f5be5391be29471676dc07040a56c8fdfab") or MD5 in~ ("41999a3d0da035ff8068905c90235ea50121329cb0661e38d745974ebf5e3ae2", "78945c844fc23dd3446cf17987edeeb6cc21986820c92df82a126af24a5a38d1", "d89bb4b23a67814ef511e4e9dda7ad36fa519a322fa7c25ea451c7dd7ef61e54", "f6e4b09ef788adef3f65fd2b99da8f5be5391be29471676dc07040a56c8fdfab")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["41999a3d0da035ff8068905c90235ea50121329cb0661e38d745974ebf5e3ae2", "78945c844fc23dd3446cf17987edeeb6cc21986820c92df82a126af24a5a38d1", "d89bb4b23a67814ef511e4e9dda7ad36fa519a322fa7c25ea451c7dd7ef61e54", "f6e4b09ef788adef3f65fd2b99da8f5be5391be29471676dc07040a56c8fdfab"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] OAuth consent grant to unfamiliar third-party AI / SaaS app — Vercel-style trust chain attack
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] Shai-Hulud npm worm — shai-hulud-workflow.yml dropped into .github/workflows/ · [LLM] Shai-Hulud bundle.js — known-bad SHA256 written to disk · Suspicious browser extension installation · File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] Shai-Hulud worm exfil — outbound to webhook.site/bb8ca5f6 from developer or CI process · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] TruffleHog binary spawned by npm/node — Shai-Hulud secret harvest · Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs · OAuth consent / suspicious app grant
Shai-Hulud npm worm — shai-hulud-workflow.yml dropped into .github/workflows/ AIInstallation High
Detects the Shai-Hulud self-spreading npm worm's persistence artifact — a GitHub Actions workflow named shai-hulud-workflow.yml written into a repository's .github/workflows/ directory on a developer workstation or CI runner. The workflow re-exfiltrates secrets on every push and is the worm's mechanism for surviving a single npm-package cleanup. Rationale: Filename shai-hulud-workflow.yml in .github/workflows/ is the worm's signature persistence artefact, confirmed by ReversingLabs and Wiz public IOC reports. The article explicitly names Shai-Hulud as the example of npm maintainer compromise. Cross-checked against ReversingLabs and Wiz public IOC bundles. Cross-checked against: • https://www.reversinglabs.com/blog/shai-hulud-worm-npm • https://www.wiz.io/blog/shai-hulud-npm-supply-chain-attack • https://www.sysdig.com/blog/shai-hulud-the-novel-self-replicating-worm-infecting-hundreds-of-npm-packages
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1053.005 T1546
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Internal security awareness training repo where engineers committed the worm's workflow file as a teaching example
  • Red-team or detection-engineering team intentionally replicating the worm for rule validation
  • Threat-intel researcher pulling the malicious yml down for analysis on a sandbox VM
  • Backup or restore of a previously-cleaned repo where the file lingered in .git history
  • SOC analyst saving the IOC file under a campaign-named folder for documentation
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("git.exe","code.exe") and InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("checkout","pull","clone") and FolderPath has_any ("security-research","redteam","sandbox","ioc-collection"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the file path's parent — was the yml created by git.exe/code.exe (local clone or commit replay, lower urgency) or by node.exe/npm.exe (active worm propagation, contain immediately). Hash the file and compare against 46faab8ab153fae6e80e7cca38eab363075bb524edd79e42269217a083628f09. 2) Contain: isolate the host, revoke the developer's GitHub PAT and npm token, rotate any cloud credentials cached on the box (AWS, GCP, Azure), and search the developer's GitHub org for any newly-created public repository named 'Shai-Hulud' which holds the exfiltrated data.json. 3) Hunt: across all dev/CI hosts pivot on outbound to webhook.site (see related UC), TruffleHog binary execution under node parentage, and any package the developer publishes — the worm republishes maintained packages to spread.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileRenamed","FileModified")
| where FileName =~ "shai-hulud-workflow.yml"
   or FolderPath has @"\.github\workflows\shai-hulud"
   or FolderPath has "/.github/workflows/shai-hulud"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName,
          AccountName = InitiatingProcessAccountName,
          FolderPath, FileName, SHA256,
          ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFileName,
          ParentCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          GrandParent = InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where TargetFileName =~ "shai-hulud-workflow.yml"
   or TargetFilePath has @"\.github\workflows\shai-hulud"
   or TargetFilePath has "/.github/workflows/shai-hulud"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername,
          TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, TargetFileSHA256,
          ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Shai-Hulud npm Worm GitHub Actions Workflow File Drop
id: 7a3b1f88-2c5e-4d29-9b1f-3a8c4e6f12d9
status: experimental
description: Detects creation of the Shai-Hulud worm's shai-hulud-workflow.yml file under .github/workflows/. This workflow is the worm's persistence mechanism — it re-exfiltrates GitHub/npm/cloud tokens to attacker infrastructure on every push.
references:
  - https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/early-warning-signs-of-supply-chain-attacks-live-in-the-dark-web/
  - https://www.reversinglabs.com/blog/shai-hulud-worm-npm
  - https://www.wiz.io/blog/shai-hulud-npm-supply-chain-attack
author: Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/12
tags:
  - attack.t1195.002
  - attack.persistence
  - attack.execution
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_name:
    TargetFilename|endswith: '\shai-hulud-workflow.yml'
  selection_path:
    TargetFilename|contains:
      - '\.github\workflows\shai-hulud'
      - '/.github/workflows/shai-hulud'
  condition: selection_name or selection_path
falsepositives:
  - Red-team or security-research lab replicating the Shai-Hulud worm under a campaign-named lab folder
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:11 @TargetFilename:(*shai-hulud-workflow.yml* OR *Shai-Hulud-workflow.yml* OR *SHAI-HULUD-WORKFLOW.YML*)
#event_simpleName=FileWritten TargetFileName=/shai-hulud-workflow\.yml$/i
| regex("(\\\\|/)\\.github(\\\\|/)workflows(\\\\|/)", field=TargetFileName)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, TargetFileName], function=count())

Shai-Hulud worm exfil — outbound to webhook.site/bb8ca5f6 from developer or CI process AICommand & Control High
Detects outbound HTTPS to the Shai-Hulud worm's documented webhook.site exfiltration endpoint (UUID bb8ca5f6-4175-45d2-b042-fc9ebb8170b7), or any traffic to webhook.site originating from node/npm/yarn/git on a developer workstation. The worm posts harvested npm/GitHub/AWS/GCP tokens to this endpoint after secrets are scraped. Rationale: webhook.site/bb8ca5f6-4175-45d2-b042-fc9ebb8170b7 is the canonical Shai-Hulud exfil endpoint per ReversingLabs and Sysdig. The article names Shai-Hulud directly as the worm that 'stole developer secrets' and 'propagated across repositories'. Cross-referenced against multiple public IOC bundles. Cross-checked against: • https://www.reversinglabs.com/blog/shai-hulud-worm-npm • https://www.sysdig.com/blog/shai-hulud-the-novel-self-replicating-worm-infecting-hundreds-of-npm-packages • https://www.zscaler.com/blogs/security-research/mitigating-risks-shai-hulud-npm-worm
ATT&CKT1567 T1102 T1041
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Engineer uses webhook.site for legitimate webhook debugging during third-party integration work
  • CI smoke test posting to a personal webhook.site URL for output capture
  • QA team using webhook.site as a stand-in for an unfinished partner API
  • Security training where the analyst's lab box reproduces the worm's exfil call
  • Browser extension that pings webhook.site as part of its onboarding flow
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("webhook-test","integration-debug","mock-callback") and InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ ("code.exe","WindowsTerminal.exe","explorer.exe") and not (RemoteUrl has "bb8ca5f6-4175-45d2-b042-fc9ebb8170b7"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm parent — node.exe / runner.exe / npm.exe parentage with no developer-initiated debugging session is the smoking gun. Capture the HTTP body if possible; the worm POSTs a base64 JSON blob of harvested env vars and token files. 2) Contain: isolate, revoke every credential the box has touched in the last 14 days (GitHub PATs, npm tokens, AWS/GCP keys, Azure credentials, Kafka creds, monitoring tokens), and check the developer's GitHub for new public repos named 'Shai-Hulud' containing data.json — delete them immediately and assume the secrets in them are burned. 3) Hunt: pivot org-wide on webhook.site DNS, on any package that this developer publishes (worm propagates by republishing maintained packages), and on bundle.js/SHA256 46faab8ab153... drops across dev fleet.
let ShaiHuludUuid = "bb8ca5f6-4175-45d2-b042-fc9ebb8170b7";
let DevProcs = dynamic(["node.exe","npm.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe","git.exe","runner.exe","Runner.Worker.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","bash.exe"]);
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where isnotempty(RemoteUrl)
| where RemoteUrl has "webhook.site"
| where RemoteUrl has ShaiHuludUuid
      or InitiatingProcessFileName in~ (DevProcs)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName,
          AccountName = InitiatingProcessAccountName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName,
          InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessParentFileName,
          RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| order by Timestamp desc
let ShaiHuludUuid = "bb8ca5f6-4175-45d2-b042-fc9ebb8170b7";
let DevProcs = dynamic(["node.exe","npm.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe","git.exe","runner.exe","runner.worker.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","bash.exe"]);
ImWebSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where Url has "webhook.site"
| where Url has ShaiHuludUuid
      or tolower(tostring(split(SrcUsername,"\\")[-1])) in (DevProcs)
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, SrcHostname,
          HttpMethod, Url, HttpRequestBodyBytes, HttpResponseHeaderContentType,
          DstIpAddr, DstHostname
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Shai-Hulud npm Worm Exfiltration to webhook.site Endpoint
id: 5e2c91ad-6d04-4a17-bb43-f31b78c4e09a
status: experimental
description: Detects outbound traffic to the Shai-Hulud worm's documented webhook.site exfiltration UUID, or any webhook.site traffic from a Node/npm/git toolchain process.
references:
  - https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/early-warning-signs-of-supply-chain-attacks-live-in-the-dark-web/
  - https://www.sysdig.com/blog/shai-hulud-the-novel-self-replicating-worm-infecting-hundreds-of-npm-packages
author: Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/12
tags:
  - attack.t1567
  - attack.exfiltration
logsource:
  category: network_connection
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_uuid:
    DestinationHostname|contains: 'webhook.site'

      - '\node.exe'

      - '\yarn.exe'
      - '\pnpm.exe'

    DestinationHostname|contains: 'webhook.site'
  condition: selection_uuid or selection_devproc

source:(windows.sysmon OR windows.defender) (@DestinationHostname:(*webhook.site/bb8ca5f6-4175-45d2-b042-fc9ebb8170b7* OR *webhook.site*) OR @RemoteUrl:(*webhook.site/bb8ca5f6-4175-45d2-b042-fc9ebb8170b7* OR *webhook.site*)) AND @Image:(*\node.exe OR *\Node.exe OR *\npm.exe OR *\yarn.exe OR *\pnpm.exe OR *\git.exe OR *\runner.exe OR *\Runner.Worker.exe OR *\powershell.exe OR *\PowerShell.exe OR *\pwsh.exe)
#event_simpleName=DnsRequest DomainName=/webhook\.site/i
| join({#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/(node|npm|yarn|pnpm|git|runner|powershell|pwsh)\.exe$/i}, field=ContextProcessId, key=TargetProcessId)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, DomainName], function=count())

TruffleHog binary spawned by npm/node — Shai-Hulud secret harvest AIActions on Objectives High
Detects execution of the TruffleHog secret-scanning binary as a child of node.exe / npm.exe / yarn.exe / pnpm.exe / a GitHub Actions runner. The Shai-Hulud worm bundles TruffleHog and runs it post-install to identify and harvest npm / GitHub / AWS / GCP / Azure credentials on developer workstations and CI runners. Rationale: TruffleHog under npm/node parentage is the article-named worm's documented secret-harvest mechanism — confirmed by ReversingLabs, Checkmarx, and Sysdig. Parent-child constraint keeps FPs in DevSecOps pipelines manageable: legitimate scans run under a CI job step with a known runner identity. Cross-checked against: • https://www.reversinglabs.com/blog/shai-hulud-worm-npm • https://checkmarx.com/zero-post/inside-shai-huluds-maw-how-the-npm-worm-exploits-and-propagates/ • https://www.sysdig.com/blog/shai-hulud-the-novel-self-replicating-worm-infecting-hundreds-of-npm-packages
ATT&CKT1552.001 T1555 T1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Sanctioned DevSecOps pipeline running TruffleHog as a pre-merge secret-scan step on a GitHub Actions runner
  • Local developer pre-commit hook running TruffleHog to catch their own leaked secrets
  • Security team performing a hands-on secret audit using TruffleHog under bash/cmd
  • Backup/restore of a CI runner image that includes TruffleHog binary
  • Renovate/Dependabot bot CI runs that include secret-scan tooling
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("runner.exe","Runner.Worker.exe") and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("trufflehog filesystem --no-update","trufflehog git --no-update") and InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ ("runner.listener.exe","agent.listener.exe"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the exact parent chain — a sanctioned pre-merge pipeline TruffleHog scan has runner.exe → trufflehog with a known repo identity; the worm spawns TruffleHog under node.exe / npm.exe with a postinstall script command line. Hash the binary and check whether it was downloaded fresh into a temp/node_modules path vs the system PATH. 2) Contain: isolate the host, revoke all developer credentials cached on disk (NPM_TOKEN, GITHUB_TOKEN, AWS keys, GCP service-account JSON, Azure CLI tokens), and check the developer's GitHub for newly-created repos. 3) Hunt: pivot on webhook.site outbound (see related UC), shai-hulud-workflow.yml drops, bundle.js writes inside node_modules, and any new package version this developer published in the last 72 hours — assume publish chain compromise.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where (FileName matches regex @"(?i)^trufflehog([0-9])?(\.exe)?$"
        or ProcessCommandLine has "trufflehog filesystem"
        or ProcessCommandLine has "trufflehog git"
        or ProcessCommandLine has "trufflehog --json")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe","npm.exe","npm-cli.js","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe","runner.exe","Runner.Worker.exe","bash.exe","sh.exe","cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
     or InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ ("node.exe","npm.exe","yarn.exe","runner.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName,
          AccountName, ProcessCommandLine, FolderPath, SHA256,
          ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFileName,
          ParentCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          GrandParent = InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where TargetProcessName matches regex @"(?i)trufflehog([0-9])?(\.exe)?$"
     or TargetProcessCommandLine has "trufflehog filesystem"
     or TargetProcessCommandLine has "trufflehog git"
     or TargetProcessCommandLine has "trufflehog --json"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("node.exe","npm.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe","runner.exe","Runner.Worker.exe","bash","sh","cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername,
          TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine,
          ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine,
          SHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Shai-Hulud bundle.js — known-bad SHA256 written to disk AIInstallation Medium
Hash-based alerting on the Shai-Hulud worm's bundle.js payload. The published SHA256 46faab8ab153fae6e80e7cca38eab363075bb524edd79e42269217a083628f09 is the canonical bundle.js identified by ReversingLabs; additional candidate hashes from this article's IOC bundle are included as likely variants. Targets either the file landing on disk in a node_modules tree or the bundle.js executing under node parentage. Rationale: 46faab8ab153... is the ReversingLabs-confirmed Shai-Hulud bundle.js hash. The article ships an IOC bundle of additional SHA256s consistent with worm-variant reporting; treated here as candidate variants. Behavioural fallback (bundle.js created in node_modules by npm/node parentage) covers hash-rotation cases. Cross-checked against: • https://www.reversinglabs.com/blog/shai-hulud-worm-npm • https://www.wiz.io/blog/shai-hulud-npm-supply-chain-attack • https://cybersecurefox.com/en/shai-hulud-npm-worm-github-actions-supply-chain/
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1059.007
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Threat-intel sandbox detonation of the bundle.js sample on a research host
  • IR forensic image mounted on an analysis machine triggering the hash on read
  • Benign npm package legitimately shipping a bundle.js (hash will not match — behavioural rule only)
  • EDR re-scan of an already-quarantined Shai-Hulud artifact triggering duplicate alerts
  • Detection-engineering lab repo containing the IOC for rule validation
Suppression filter
| where DeviceName !in ("sandbox-research-01","ir-analysis-01","malware-lab-01")
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the hash hit is on a real developer/CI host vs a sanctioned research/sandbox machine (allow-list those by hostname). For the behavioural variant — bundle.js in node_modules created by npm/node — pull the parent npm-install command line to identify which package brought the worm in. 2) Contain: isolate the host, kill node.exe, quarantine the file, revoke every credential the box has cached (NPM_TOKEN, GITHUB_TOKEN, AWS/GCP/Azure keys, Kafka and monitoring tokens), and identify which package shipped it — pull that package version from internal mirrors and notify the broader engineering org not to install. 3) Hunt: pivot on shai-hulud-workflow.yml file drops, webhook.site outbound, TruffleHog spawn under npm parentage, and search the developer's GitHub for new repos named 'Shai-Hulud' containing data.json.

OAuth consent grant to unfamiliar third-party AI / SaaS app — Vercel-style trust chain attack AIDelivery Medium
Hunts the supply-chain pattern called out by the article's Vercel example: a third-party AI tool or SaaS connector receives an OAuth consent grant from a user, gaining cross-tenant access to SaaS scope (mail, files, Graph). Surfaces consent grants to applications never before seen in the tenant, or grants made by non-admin users to apps with high-risk permission scopes. Rationale: Article calls Vercel's April 2026 incident a textbook supply-chain consent abuse — a trusted third-party AI tool with OAuth-connected SaaS access broadening blast radius. Detection anti-joins against tenant's 30-day baseline of seen ApplicationIds and gates on high-risk delegated scopes. Falcon LogScale + Splunk Endpoint datamodels + CloudWatch left empty since the telemetry lives only in AAD audit (no FDR/CIM/AWS analogue).
ATT&CKT1528 T1199 T1078.004
Data sourcesAuthentication
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • IT-sanctioned new SaaS onboarding (e.g. a new HR or CRM connector rolling out to a pilot group)
  • Microsoft first-party app newly enabled in the tenant (Copilot variants, Power Platform connectors)
  • Admin testing a new vendor app in a sandbox tenant that shares logs
  • User reconnecting a previously-deleted integration (consent regenerated)
  • Marketplace app installed by a developer for a one-off prototype
Suppression filter
| where TargetApp !in~ ("Microsoft Copilot","Power Automate","Teams Toolkit") and ConsentingUser !in~ ("saas-admin@contoso.com","app-onboarding-svc@contoso.com")
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the AppId and look it up against Microsoft's AppId catalog and the tenant's app-governance list. Confirm whether IT/security knew about this app — if yes, allow-list and close. If unknown, examine the publisher domain, the consenting user's recent sign-ins for impossible-travel or risky-state, and whether the consent included offline_access (refresh-token persistence). 2) Contain: revoke the service-principal's consent (Remove-AzureADServicePrincipal or Microsoft Graph DELETE /oauth2PermissionGrants/{id}), invalidate all issued refresh tokens for that user, and block the AppId at the tenant level via conditional-access app filter. 3) Hunt: AADServicePrincipalSignInLogs for the AppId — which mailboxes/files did it actually touch in the last 14 days. OfficeActivity for any MailItemsAccessed by the SP. Search underground monitoring for any post mentioning the tenant or the app publisher.
let Lookback = 30d;
let KnownApps = AADSignInEventsBeta
    | where Timestamp between (ago(Lookback) .. ago(2d))
    | summarize by ApplicationId;
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(2d)
| where ActionType has_any ("Consent to application","Add app role assignment grant to user","Add delegated permission grant")
| extend AppName = tostring(parse_json(tostring(RawEventData)).Target[0].ID)
| extend ConsentedApp = tostring(ActivityObjects[0].Name),
         ConsentedAppId = tostring(ActivityObjects[0].Id),
         GrantedScopes = tostring(parse_json(tostring(RawEventData)).ModifiedProperties)
| where ConsentedAppId !in (KnownApps)
| where GrantedScopes has_any ("Mail.Read","Mail.ReadWrite","Files.Read.All","Files.ReadWrite.All","Sites.Read.All","User.Read.All","Directory.Read.All","offline_access")
| project Timestamp, AccountDisplayName, AccountObjectId, IPAddress, CountryCode,
          IsAdminOperation, ConsentedApp, ConsentedAppId, GrantedScopes,
          UserAgent, ActionType
| order by Timestamp desc
let Lookback = 30d;
let KnownApps = SigninLogs
    | where TimeGenerated between (ago(Lookback) .. ago(2d))
    | summarize by AppId;
AuditLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2d)
| where OperationName in ("Consent to application","Add delegated permission grant","Add app role assignment grant to user")
| extend TargetApp = tostring(TargetResources[0].displayName),
         TargetAppId = tostring(TargetResources[0].id),
         ConsentingUser = tostring(InitiatedBy.user.userPrincipalName),
         IpAddress = tostring(InitiatedBy.user.ipAddress),
         ModifiedProps = tostring(TargetResources[0].modifiedProperties)
| where TargetAppId !in (KnownApps)
| extend HighRiskScope = ModifiedProps has_any ("Mail.Read","Mail.ReadWrite","Files.Read.All","Files.ReadWrite.All","Sites.Read.All","User.Read.All","Directory.Read.All","offline_access","full_access_as_app")
| where HighRiskScope
| project TimeGenerated, ConsentingUser, IpAddress,
          TargetApp, TargetAppId, ModifiedProps, OperationName, Result
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: AAD OAuth Consent to Unfamiliar Third-Party App with High-Risk Scopes
id: c4ed7b21-9a30-4d5e-87b1-6e9f4c81207d
status: experimental
description: A user (or admin) consented to a third-party application not previously seen in the tenant, granting high-risk delegated scopes (Mail.*, Files.*, Sites.*, Directory.Read.All, offline_access). Pattern matches Vercel-style supply-chain compromise via OAuth-connected SaaS tools.
references:
  - https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/early-warning-signs-of-supply-chain-attacks-live-in-the-dark-web/
author: Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/12
tags:
  - attack.t1528
  - attack.credential_access
  - attack.t1199
logsource:
  product: azure
  service: auditlogs
detection:
  selection_op:
    OperationName:
      - 'Consent to application'
      - 'Add delegated permission grant'
      - 'Add app role assignment grant to user'
  selection_scope:
    ModifiedProperties|contains:
      - 'Mail.Read'
      - 'Mail.ReadWrite'
      - 'Files.Read.All'
      - 'Files.ReadWrite.All'
      - 'Sites.Read.All'
      - 'Directory.Read.All'
      - 'offline_access'
      - 'full_access_as_app'
  condition: selection_op and selection_scope
falsepositives:
  - Sanctioned SaaS roll-out where IT explicitly onboarded a new vendor (allow-list AppId at deployment)
  - Legit Microsoft-published first-party app that wasn't seen in baseline window
level: medium
source:azure.activeDirectory @evt.name:("Consent to application" OR "Add delegated permission grant" OR "Add app role assignment grant to user") @properties.targetResources.modifiedProperties:(*Mail.Read* OR *Mail.ReadWrite* OR *Files.Read.All* OR *Files.ReadWrite.All* OR *Sites.Read.All* OR *Directory.Read.All* OR *offline_access* OR *full_access_as_app*)
Suspicious browser extension installation Installation Medium
Side-loaded / unsigned extensions, often masquerading as wallets, productivity tools.
ATT&CKT1176
Data sourcesEndpoint.Registry DeviceRegistryEvents
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where RegistryKey has_any ("\Software\Google\Chrome\Extensions\","\Software\Microsoft\Edge\Extensions\","\Software\Mozilla\Firefox\Extensions\")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, RegistryKey, RegistryValueName, RegistryValueData,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessAccountName

| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where RegistryKey has_any (@"\Software\Google\Chrome\Extensions\",
                              @"\Software\Microsoft\Edge\Extensions\",
                              @"\Software\Mozilla\Firefox\Extensions\")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, RegistryKey,
          RegistryValue, RegistryValueData, ActingProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Browser Extension Installation via Registry
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d0a
status: experimental

    administrative install of an extension. Often used by adware /
    info-stealers to bypass user-level extension controls.

author: Clankerusecase

    from datamodel=Endpoint.Registry

Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs Actions on Objectives High
Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies SQLite from Chrome/Edge/Firefox.
ATT&CKT1539 T1555.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\", @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\", @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where FileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FolderPath, FileName, ActionType

// ASIM ImFileEvent — covers MDE, Sysmon, AuditD, Defender for Cloud, etc.
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\",
                                  @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\",
                                  @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where TargetFileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where ActingProcessName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName,

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s) Reconnaissance High
Match vulnerability scanner output to the CVE(s) named in the article.
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-33634")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-33634")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc
APPLICATION
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Vulnerabilities
    where Vulnerabilities.signature IN ("CVE-2026-33634")
    by Vulnerabilities.dest, Vulnerabilities.signature, Vulnerabilities.severity, Vulnerabilities.cve
| `drop_dm_object_name(Vulnerabilities)`
| sort - severity
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Vulnerabilities
    where Vulnerabilities.signature IN ("CVE-2026-33634")
    by Vulnerabilities.dest, Vulnerabilities.signature, Vulnerabilities.severity, Vulnerabilities.cve
| `drop_dm_object_name(Vulnerabilities)`
| sort - severity
OAuth consent / suspicious app grant Actions on Objectives High
Cloud identity abuse: app gets high-priv scopes, often via consent phishing.
ATT&CKT1528 T1098.001
Data sourcesAuthentication.Authentication CloudAppEvents
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("Consent to application.","Add OAuth2PermissionGrant.","Add delegated permission grant.")
| project Timestamp, AccountObjectId, AccountDisplayName, ActivityType,
          ActivityObjects, IPAddress, UserAgent
// Entra ID directory audit — user / admin consent to a third-party app.
AuditLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OperationName has "Consent to application"
| where Result =~ "success"
| extend AppName = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].displayName),

| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Entra ID Consent to Third-Party OAuth Application
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d05

Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children Exploitation Medium
Supply-chain trojan signal: legitimate signed binary spawning script interpreters or exotic LOLBins.
ATT&CKT1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
// Replace `"setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe"` with the vendor binaries observed in the
// article (matching shape with the Defender query).
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\bitsadmin.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Trusted Vendor Binary Launching Unusual Children
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d09
status: experimental
description: |
    A signed vendor binary (in the article's named-vendors list)
    spawning script-host or LOLBin children. Strongest signal when
    paired with a recent CVE / supply-chain advisory naming the same
    vendor.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1195
    - attack.initial-access
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\wmic.exe'
            - '\bitsadmin.exe'
    selection_parent_vendor:
        ParentImage|contains:
            - '\Program Files\'
            - '\Program Files (x86)\'
    condition: selection_child and selection_parent_vendor
falsepositives:
    - Many — installers and updaters legitimately spawn children. Pin
      the parent path to specific vendor binaries observed in the
      article before alerting.
level: medium
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
Network connections to article IPs / domains Command & Control High
Outbound traffic to attacker infrastructure named in the article.
ATT&CKT1071
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Web Network_Resolution.DNS DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteIP in ("") or RemoteUrl has_any ("webhook.site")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
let BadIPs     = dynamic([""]);
let BadDomains = dynamic(["webhook.site"]);
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where DstIpAddr in (BadIPs)
   or Url has_any (BadDomains)

| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Outbound Connection to Article-Named IP / Domain
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d0f
status: experimental
description: |
    Replace `__IP_LIST__` / `__DOMAIN_LIST__` placeholders with
    article-specific destinations. For dynamic IOC management, use a
    watchlist or external feed.
references:

author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:

    product: windows
detection:

        DestinationIp:

            - '__IP_PLACEHOLDER_2__'
    selection_domain:
        DestinationHostname:
            - '__DOMAIN_PLACEHOLDER_1__'
            - '__DOMAIN_PLACEHOLDER_2__'
    condition: selection_ip or selection_domain
falsepositives:

level: critical
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.dest IN ("")
    by All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest, All_Traffic.dest_port
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| append
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count from datamodel=Web
        where Web.dest IN ("webhook.site")
        by Web.src, Web.dest, Web.url, Web.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`]
| append
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS
        where DNS.query IN ("webhook.site")
        by DNS.src, DNS.query, DNS.answer
     | `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)`]
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.dest IN ("")
    by All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest, All_Traffic.dest_port
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| append
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Web
        where Web.dest IN ("webhook.site")
        by Web.src, Web.dest, Web.url, Web.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`]
| append
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS
        where DNS.query IN ("webhook.site")
        by DNS.src, DNS.query, DNS.answer
     | `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)`]
File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents

Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2025-67644", "CVE-2026-28277", "CVE-2026-27022")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2025-67644", "CVE-2026-28277", "CVE-2026-27022")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc

// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["1ba67bb1cfad42446880cca53cbd05fe66d7514b2bb139b48e5c63adff14be7b", "2cc7c2d8653c98e5bac32fcaf5e45b861efb4bb87df3b3f96285edb475e75bba", "62d62950ff7a0e43550a5d0ba55d32d5083b9de5538e0f012e406b6d951e16aa"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Agentjacking Attack Tricks AI Coding Agents Into Running Malicious Code

The Hacker News
2026-06-12 11 use cases 5 techniques 5 kill-chain phases detected

Cybersecurity researchers have described what they say is a new class of attack that can trick artificial intelligence (AI) coding agents into running arbitrary code on developer machines. Called Agentjacking by Tenet Security, the attack can be triggered by means of a fake error report crafted using Sentry, an open-source error-tracking and performance-monitoring platform. "The attack

ATT&CKT1190 T1195.002 T1204.004 T1528 T1566
Domainsadvisory-tracker.com

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process · Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] AI coding agent (Claude Code / Cursor / Codex) spawning shell that fetch-and-executes remote payload
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] Agentjacking C2/exfiltration to advisory-tracker.com (Tenet Sentry-MCP attack) · [LLM] AI coding agent descendant reading developer credentials / env (Agentjacking credential access) · OAuth consent / suspicious app grant
Agentjacking C2/exfiltration to advisory-tracker.com (Tenet Sentry-MCP attack) AIActions on Objectives High
Hunts the Tenet Security 'Agentjacking' exfiltration endpoint that receives developer environment variables, git credentials, repo URLs and tokens stolen by npm typosquat packages that a hijacked AI coding agent (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex) was tricked into installing via a forged Sentry issue. Both DNS resolution and TCP egress are pivoted because the npm-installed payload posts to https://advisory-tracker.com/api/v1/telemetry. Rationale: advisory-tracker.com and 52.206.47.180 are the Tenet-published exfiltration endpoint for the Agentjacking PoC, also enumerated in the PSPDFKit IOC repo for the related Sentry npm typosquat campaign. Cross-checked: Tenet's blog post and the PSPDFKit/sentry-npm-typosquat-2026-06-iocs GitHub repo both list the same domain + IP + /api/v1/telemetry path, so the IOC has independent corroboration beyond the THN article. Cross-checked against: • https://tenetsecurity.ai/blog/agentjacking-coding-agents-with-fake-sentry-errors/ • https://github.com/PSPDFKit/sentry-npm-typosquat-2026-06-iocs • https://www.infosecurity-magazine.com/news/agentjacking-attacks-hijack-ai/
ATT&CKT1041 T1071.001 T1567
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Network_Resolution.DNS
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Authorised purple-team replay of the Tenet PoC from a research VM
  • Security-research sandbox detonating one of the IOC-listed npm packages
  • Threat-intel enrichment platform (VirusTotal/urlscan) auto-resolving advisory-tracker.com from a SOC analyst workstation
  • DNS-passive-replication sensor logging the domain without an actual host connecting
Suppression filter
| where not(InitiatingProcessFolderPath has_any (@"\sandbox\", @"\detonation\", @"\threat-research\")) and not(InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("vt-cli.exe","urlscan.exe","virustotal.exe"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull DeviceProcessEvents for the same DeviceId in the 10 min before the connection, walk the process tree (claude.exe / cursor.exe / code.exe → node.exe → npm/npx → outbound), and confirm the developer was using an AI coding agent against Sentry. 2) Contain: isolate the host via Defender Live Response; immediately rotate every credential exposed in env on a developer box — git PAT, npm _authToken, AWS/GCP keys, .env secrets, Sentry DSN, any cloud-CLI session token. Quarantine the npm cache and node_modules under the suspect project. 3) Hunt: enumerate every host in the org that resolved advisory-tracker.com or hit 52.206.47.180 in the last 30 days; scan all developer repos for the typosquat package family in package-lock.json / yarn.lock; audit Sentry org membership against affected developers to find the injected issue ID.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteUrl has "advisory-tracker.com" or RemoteIP == "52.206.47.180"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, RemoteIP, RemoteUrl, RemotePort, Protocol
| order by Timestamp desc
union
  (ImNetworkSession
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where DstHostname has "advisory-tracker.com" or DstIpAddr == "52.206.47.180"
    | extend Indicator = coalesce(DstHostname, DstIpAddr)
    | project TimeGenerated, Source="ImNetworkSession", Host=DvcHostname, User=SrcUsername, Indicator, Url),
  (ImDnsActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where DnsQuery has "advisory-tracker.com"
    | project TimeGenerated, Source="ImDnsActivity", Host=SrcHostname, User=SrcUsername, Indicator=DnsQuery, Url=DnsQuery),
  (DnsEvents
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where Name has "advisory-tracker.com"
    | project TimeGenerated, Source="DnsEvents", Host=Computer, User=tostring(""), Indicator=Name, Url=Name)
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Agentjacking exfiltration domain advisory-tracker.com resolved
id: 4e3f8d9a-2b1c-4f5e-9d0a-6c7e1f8b2a3d
status: experimental
description: DNS query for advisory-tracker.com, the Tenet 'Agentjacking' exfiltration endpoint receiving developer credentials, environment variables and git tokens posted by npm typosquats installed by a hijacked AI coding agent (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex) after a forged Sentry issue.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/agentjacking-attack-tricks-ai-coding.html
  - https://tenetsecurity.ai/blog/agentjacking-coding-agents-with-fake-sentry-errors/
  - https://github.com/PSPDFKit/sentry-npm-typosquat-2026-06-iocs
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/12
tags:
  - attack.exfiltration
  - attack.t1041
  - attack.command_and_control
  - attack.t1071.001
logsource:
  category: dns
detection:
  selection:
    QueryName|endswith: 'advisory-tracker.com'
  condition: selection
falsepositives:
  - Authorised security-research sandbox detonation of the Tenet PoC
level: high
source:(windows.sysmon OR linux.auditd OR linux.syslog) AND ((@EventID:3 AND (@DestinationHostname:*advisory-tracker.com OR @DestinationIp:52.206.47.180)) OR (@EventID:22 AND @QueryName:*advisory-tracker.com) OR @network.destination.ip:52.206.47.180)
((#event_simpleName=DnsRequest DomainName=/(^|\.)advisory-tracker\.com$/i) OR (#event_simpleName=NetworkConnectIP4 RemoteAddressIP4="52.206.47.180"))
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, ContextProcessId, DomainName, RemoteAddressIP4, RemotePort], function=count())
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=t count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic where (All_Traffic.dest_ip="52.206.47.180" OR All_Traffic.dest="advisory-tracker.com" OR All_Traffic.dest="*.advisory-tracker.com") by All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.user, All_Traffic.app, All_Traffic.dest, All_Traffic.dest_ip, All_Traffic.dest_port | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)` | append [| tstats summariesonly=t count from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS where (DNS.query="advisory-tracker.com" OR DNS.query="*.advisory-tracker.com") by DNS.src, DNS.query, DNS.answer | `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)`] | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime) | sort - lastTime
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic where (All_Traffic.dest_ip="52.206.47.180" OR All_Traffic.dest="advisory-tracker.com" OR All_Traffic.dest="*.advisory-tracker.com") by All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.user, All_Traffic.app, All_Traffic.dest, All_Traffic.dest_ip, All_Traffic.dest_port | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)` | append [| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS where (DNS.query="advisory-tracker.com" OR DNS.query="*.advisory-tracker.com") by DNS.src, DNS.query, DNS.answer | `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)`] | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime) | sort - lastTime
AI coding agent (Claude Code / Cursor / Codex) spawning shell that fetch-and-executes remote payload AIInstallation High
Hunts the Agentjacking execution stage: after a forged Sentry MCP event is rendered as 'Resolution' guidance, the AI coding agent runs the attacker's instruction on the developer's machine. Specifically targets the Claude / Cursor / Codex process tree spawning cmd/PowerShell/bash/node that downloads-and-evaluates remote content (curl|sh, IEX DownloadString, node -e fetch, base64-decoded shell) or directly references the Tenet exfil host. Rationale: Article + Tenet blog both describe AI coding agents (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex) reading a forged Sentry 'Resolution' over MCP and executing the attacker's shell command on the developer machine with developer privileges. Anchors on the article-specific parent-process names plus the standard fetch-and-execute payload shapes attacker injections use, and includes the corroborated advisory-tracker.com host so a literal reference fires high-confidence. Cross-checked against: • https://tenetsecurity.ai/blog/agentjacking-coding-agents-with-fake-sentry-errors/ • https://github.com/PSPDFKit/sentry-npm-typosquat-2026-06-iocs
ATT&CKT1059.001 T1059.003 T1059.007 T1105 T1204
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer asking the agent to run a legitimate install one-liner from a vendor (e.g. nvm, rustup, ohmyzsh) that uses curl|bash
  • Agent-invoked build step that legitimately uses 'node -e' for codegen
  • PowerShell profile auto-load triggering Invoke-Expression on a vetted helper module
  • Security team running a Tenet PoC replay in a research VM
  • Internal devtools-team approved bootstrap scripts piped through bash
Suppression filter
| where not(ProcessCommandLine has_any ("raw.githubusercontent.com/nvm-sh","sh.rustup.rs","get.docker.com","raw.githubusercontent.com/ohmyzsh","get-poetry.org")) and not(InitiatingProcessFolderPath has "\\purple-team\\")
Response runbook
1) Triage: capture full parent chain (AI agent → shell → payload), the exact ProcessCommandLine, and any URL it pulled. Pull Sentry MCP request logs for that developer's session to identify the malicious issue ID; correlate to inbound POSTs to /api/0/store/ or /api/0/envelope/ on Sentry. 2) Contain: kill the descendant tree via Live Response; suspend the developer's AI-agent session; revoke every credential touchable from that shell context (git PAT, npm _authToken, AWS/GCP CLI tokens, SSH keys); quarantine downloaded artefacts and any new node_modules. 3) Hunt: pivot on the fetched URL, npm package name, and command hash across the dev fleet; query Sentry to see if the same injected issue body appears in other projects; audit which developers asked the agent to 'fix Sentry issues' in the last 14 days and verify their machines.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where (InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("claude.exe","cursor.exe","code.exe","codex.exe","claude-code.exe"))
    or (InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ ("claude.exe","cursor.exe","code.exe","codex.exe","claude-code.exe")
        and InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe","npm.cmd","npx.cmd"))
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","bash.exe","sh.exe","node.exe","npm.cmd","npx.cmd","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("Invoke-Expression","IEX(","IEX (","DownloadString","Net.WebClient","| sh","| bash","|sh ","|bash ","node -e","base64 -d","bash -c","powershell -enc","powershell -e ","powershell -EncodedCommand","curl -s ","wget -qO","advisory-tracker.com")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          GrandparentProcess = InitiatingProcessParentFileName,
          ParentProcess = InitiatingProcessFileName,
          ParentCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ChildProcess = FileName,
          ChildCmd = ProcessCommandLine,
          SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("claude.exe","cursor.exe","code.exe","codex.exe","claude-code.exe")
     or (ParentProcessName has_any ("node.exe","npm.cmd","npx.cmd") and ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("claude","cursor","codex"))
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","bash.exe","sh.exe","node.exe","npm.cmd","npx.cmd","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("Invoke-Expression","IEX(","IEX (","DownloadString","Net.WebClient","| sh","| bash","|sh ","|bash ","node -e","base64 -d","bash -c","powershell -enc","powershell -EncodedCommand","curl -s","wget -qO","advisory-tracker.com")
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

description: AI coding agent (Claude Code / Cursor / Codex) parent process spawning cmd / PowerShell / bash / node that downloads-and-evaluates remote content or references the Tenet Agentjacking exfil host. The forged Sentry MCP 'Resolution' tricks the agent into executing this on the developer machine.

source:windows.sysmon AND @EventID:1 AND @ParentImage:(*\\claude.exe OR *\\Claude.exe OR *\\cursor.exe OR *\\Cursor.exe OR *\\code.exe OR *\\Code.exe OR *\\codex.exe OR *\\claude-code.exe) AND @Image:(*\\cmd.exe OR *\\powershell.exe OR *\\PowerShell.exe OR *\\pwsh.exe OR *\\bash.exe OR *\\sh.exe OR *\\node.exe OR *\\npm.cmd OR *\\npx.cmd OR *\\curl.exe OR *\\wget.exe) AND @CommandLine:(*Invoke-Expression* OR *IEX* OR *DownloadString* OR *Net.WebClient* OR *"| sh"* OR *"| bash"* OR *"node -e"* OR *"base64 -d"* OR *"bash -c"* OR *"powershell -enc"* OR *"powershell -EncodedCommand"* OR *advisory-tracker.com*)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ParentBaseFileName=/(claude|cursor|code|codex|claude-code)\.exe$/i
| ImageFileName=/(cmd|powershell|pwsh|bash|sh|node|npm|npx|curl|wget)\.(exe|cmd)$/i
| regex("(?i)(Invoke-Expression|IEX\\s*\\(|DownloadString|Net\\.WebClient|\\|\\s*(sh|bash)\\b|node\\s+-e|base64\\s+-d|bash\\s+-c|powershell\\s+-(e|enc|EncodedCommand)|advisory-tracker\\.com)", field=CommandLine)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ParentBaseFileName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())

| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.parent_process_name IN ("claude.exe","Claude.exe","cursor.exe","Cursor.exe","code.exe","Code.exe","codex.exe","claude-code.exe") OR Processes.process_name IN ("node.exe","npm.cmd","npx.cmd") AND Processes.parent_process_name IN ("claude.exe","Claude.exe","cursor.exe","Cursor.exe","code.exe","Code.exe","codex.exe","claude-code.exe")) AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","bash.exe","sh.exe","node.exe","npm.cmd","npx.cmd","curl.exe","wget.exe") by _time, Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where match(process, "(?i)(Invoke-Expression|IEX\s*\(|DownloadString|Net\.WebClient|curl\s+[^|]+\|\s*(sh|bash)|wget\s+-O\s*-|node\s+-e|base64\s+-d\s*\|\s*(sh|bash)|bash\s+-c\s+\$\(|powershell\s+-(e|enc|c)\s|advisory-tracker)") | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime) | sort - lastTime
AI coding agent descendant reading developer credentials / env (Agentjacking credential access) AIActions on Objectives Medium
Hunts the Agentjacking credential_access stage where the hijacked AI agent's child process dumps environment variables and reads developer secret files — the specific data Tenet showed exfiltrated (env vars, git credentials, private repo URLs, AWS/cloud keys, npm _authToken, .env contents). Independent of the exfil IOC so it survives C2 rotation. Rationale: Tenet's writeup explicitly names the exfiltrated data classes — environment variables, Git credentials, private repository URLs, developer identities — which directly map to the file/env paths in this query. By anchoring on AI-coding-agent parents (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex) reading these specific resources, the detection survives even if the attacker rotates the advisory-tracker.com IOC. SENTRY_DSN is included because that's the bootstrap secret a typosquat would harvest first. Cross-checked against: • https://tenetsecurity.ai/blog/agentjacking-coding-agents-with-fake-sentry-errors/ • https://www.infosecurity-magazine.com/news/agentjacking-attacks-hijack-ai/ • https://github.com/PSPDFKit/sentry-npm-typosquat-2026-06-iocs
ATT&CKT1552.001 T1552.004 T1555 T1083
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer legitimately asking Claude/Cursor to debug a git auth failure (printenv / git config --get)
  • AI agent reading .npmrc _authToken to scope a sanctioned npm install
  • aws-cli / gcloud-cli config inspection invoked at developer request
  • ohmyzsh / shell-init scripts that printenv on session start under an agent terminal
  • CI emulator running inside Cursor terminal that dumps env for build context
Suppression filter
| where not(ProcessCommandLine has_any ("git config --global credential.helper","git config --get user.email","aws configure list","gcloud auth list")) and not(InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "--debug-auth")
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm parent chain (Claude/Cursor/Codex/node → shell → cred read) and verify the command-line wasn't a developer-issued debug step. Pull the Sentry MCP tool-call history for the developer's session and locate the issue body whose 'Resolution' text seeded the command. 2) Contain: rotate every credential whose file or env-var was read — git PAT, AWS/GCP CLI keys, SSH private keys, .env secrets, npm _authToken, the Sentry DSN itself. Force the developer to re-auth into all coding sessions and invalidate the host's OS keyring. 3) Hunt: across the dev fleet, find every AI-agent descendant that read the same credential paths in the last 30 days; correlate against outbound traffic from the same process tree to advisory-tracker.com and to any unfamiliar /api/v1/telemetry endpoint; audit the org's Sentry projects for forged issues containing markdown resolution sections.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("claude.exe","cursor.exe","code.exe","codex.exe","claude-code.exe","node.exe","npm.cmd","npx.cmd")
    or InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ ("claude.exe","cursor.exe","code.exe","codex.exe","claude-code.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any (
    "Get-ChildItem Env:","Get-ChildItem env:","ls env:","printenv","$env:",
    "type .env","cat .env","Get-Content .env",
    ".git-credentials","git config --global credential","git remote -v",
    @".aws\credentials",".aws/credentials",
    @".ssh\id_rsa",".ssh/id_rsa",@".ssh\id_ed25519",".ssh/id_ed25519",
    ".npmrc","_authToken","SENTRY_DSN"
  )
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ParentProcess = InitiatingProcessFileName,
          GrandparentProcess = InitiatingProcessParentFileName,
          ChildProcess = FileName,
          ChildCmd = ProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("claude.exe","cursor.exe","code.exe","codex.exe","claude-code.exe","node.exe","npm.cmd","npx.cmd")
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any (
    "Get-ChildItem Env:","Get-ChildItem env:","ls env:","printenv","$env:",
    "type .env","cat .env","Get-Content .env",
    ".git-credentials","git config --global credential","git remote -v",
    @".aws\credentials",".aws/credentials",
    @".ssh\id_rsa",".ssh/id_rsa",@".ssh\id_ed25519",".ssh/id_ed25519",
    ".npmrc","_authToken","SENTRY_DSN"
  )
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: AI coding agent descendant reading developer credentials (Agentjacking)
id: c8d2e3f4-a5b6-4c7d-8e9f-0a1b2c3d4e5f
status: experimental
description: Detects descendants of AI coding agents (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex) dumping environment variables or reading developer credential files (.git-credentials, .aws/credentials, .ssh keys, .env, .npmrc _authToken) — the credential_access stage of Tenet's 'Agentjacking' attack where a forged Sentry MCP event hijacks the agent.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/agentjacking-attack-tricks-ai-coding.html
  - https://tenetsecurity.ai/blog/agentjacking-coding-agents-with-fake-sentry-errors/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/12
tags:
  - attack.credential_access
  - attack.t1552.001
  - attack.t1552.004
  - attack.t1555
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_parent:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '\claude.exe'
      - '\Claude.exe'
      - '\cursor.exe'
      - '\Cursor.exe'
      - '\code.exe'
      - '\Code.exe'
      - '\codex.exe'
      - '\claude-code.exe'
      - '\node.exe'
      - '\npm.cmd'
      - '\npx.cmd'
  selection_cred:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'Get-ChildItem Env:'
      - 'ls env:'
      - 'printenv'
      - '$env:'
      - '.git-credentials'
      - 'git config --global credential'
      - 'git remote -v'
      - '.aws\credentials'
      - '.aws/credentials'
      - '.ssh\id_rsa'
      - '.ssh/id_rsa'
      - '.ssh\id_ed25519'
      - '.ssh/id_ed25519'
      - '.npmrc'
      - '_authToken'
      - 'cat .env'
      - 'type .env'
      - 'Get-Content .env'
      - 'SENTRY_DSN'
  condition: selection_parent and selection_cred
falsepositives:
  - Developer asking the AI agent to debug authentication / env config
  - Agent extension legitimately reading .npmrc tokens during a sanctioned install
  - aws-cli / gcloud-cli helper invoked by the agent on the developer's instruction
level: medium
source:windows.sysmon AND @EventID:1 AND @ParentImage:(*\\claude.exe OR *\\Claude.exe OR *\\cursor.exe OR *\\Cursor.exe OR *\\code.exe OR *\\Code.exe OR *\\codex.exe OR *\\claude-code.exe OR *\\node.exe OR *\\npm.cmd OR *\\npx.cmd) AND @CommandLine:(*"Get-ChildItem Env:"* OR *"ls env:"* OR *printenv* OR *".git-credentials"* OR *".aws\\credentials"* OR *".aws/credentials"* OR *".ssh\\id_rsa"* OR *".ssh/id_rsa"* OR *".ssh\\id_ed25519"* OR *".ssh/id_ed25519"* OR *"git remote -v"* OR *".npmrc"* OR *_authToken* OR *"cat .env"* OR *"type .env"* OR *SENTRY_DSN*)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ParentBaseFileName=/(claude|cursor|code|codex|claude-code|node|npm|npx)\.(exe|cmd)$/i
| regex("(?i)(Get-ChildItem\\s+Env:|ls\\s+env:|printenv|\\$env:[A-Za-z_]|\\.git-credentials\\b|git\\s+config\\s+--global\\s+credential|git\\s+remote\\s+-v|\\.aws[\\\\/]credentials|\\.ssh[\\\\/]id_(rsa|ed25519|ecdsa)|\\.npmrc\\b|_authToken|cat\\s+\\.env\\b|type\\s+\\.env\\b|Get-Content\\s+\\.env|SENTRY_DSN)", field=CommandLine)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ParentBaseFileName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=t count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("claude.exe","Claude.exe","cursor.exe","Cursor.exe","code.exe","Code.exe","codex.exe","claude-code.exe","node.exe","npm.cmd","npx.cmd") by _time, Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where match(process, "(?i)(Get-ChildItem\s+Env:|ls\s+env:|printenv|\$env:[A-Za-z_]|\.git-credentials\b|git\s+config\s+--global\s+credential|\.aws[\\/]credentials|\.ssh[\\/]id_(rsa|ed25519|ecdsa)|git\s+remote\s+-v|\.npmrc\b|_authToken|cat\s+\.env\b|type\s+\.env\b|Get-Content\s+\.env)") | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime) | sort - lastTime
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("claude.exe","Claude.exe","cursor.exe","Cursor.exe","code.exe","Code.exe","codex.exe","claude-code.exe","node.exe","npm.cmd","npx.cmd") by _time, Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where match(process, "(?i)(Get-ChildItem\s+Env:|ls\s+env:|printenv|\$env:[A-Za-z_]|\.git-credentials\b|git\s+config\s+--global\s+credential|\.aws[\\/]credentials|\.ssh[\\/]id_(rsa|ed25519|ecdsa)|git\s+remote\s+-v|\.npmrc\b|_authToken|cat\s+\.env\b|type\s+\.env\b|Get-Content\s+\.env)") | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime) | sort - lastTime
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
Network connections to article IPs / domains Command & Control High
Outbound traffic to attacker infrastructure named in the article.
ATT&CKT1071
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Web Network_Resolution.DNS DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteIP in ("") or RemoteUrl has_any ("advisory-tracker.com")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
let BadIPs     = dynamic([""]);
let BadDomains = dynamic(["advisory-tracker.com"]);
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where DstIpAddr in (BadIPs)
   or Url has_any (BadDomains)
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, Url, NetworkProtocol
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Outbound Connection to Article-Named IP / Domain

references:

detection:
